Males and females are affected equally, and can both transmit the disorder with a risk of 50% for each child of inheriting the mutant allele." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Autosomal recessive inheritance

The fontanelles gradually ossify, whereby the posterior fontanelle usually closes by eight weeks and the anterior fontanelle by the 9th to 16th month of age. Large fontanelles are diagnosed if the fontanelles are larger than age-dependent norms." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

Most embryologists believe that posterior choanal atresia results from a failure of rupture between the 35th and 38th day of fetal life of the partition which separates the bucconasal or buccopharyngeal membranes. The resultant choanal atresia may be unilateral or bilateral, bony or membranous, complete or incomplete. In over 90 per cent of cases the obstruction is bony, while in the remainder it is membranous. The bony type of atresia is commonly located 1-2 mm. anterior to the posterior edge of the hard palate, and the osseous septum varies in thickness from 1 to 10 mm. fields.label: Hyperthyroidism

fields.label: Adrenogenital syndrome
fields.definition: "Adrenogenital syndrome is also known as congenital adrenal hyperplasia, which results from disorders of steroid hormone production in the adrenal glands leading to a deficiency of cortisol. fields.label: Hyperactive renin-angiotensin system

fields.label: Elevated circulating growth hormone concentration
fields.definition: "Acromegaly is a condition resulting from overproduction of growth hormone by the pituitary gland in persons with closed epiphyses, and consists chiefly in the enlargement of the distal parts of the body. fields.label: Pseudohypoparathyroidism

fields.label: Abnormality of the hypothalamus-pituitary axis
fields.definition: "Abnormality of the pituitary gland (also known as hypophysis), which is an endocrine gland that protrudes from the bottom of the hypothalamus at the base of the brain. The pituitary gland secretes the hormones ACTH, TSH, PRL, GH, endorphins, FSH, LH, oxytocin, and antidiuretic hormone. The secretion of hormones from the anterior pituitary is under the strict control of hypothalamic hormones, and the posterior pituitary is essentially an extension of the hypothalamus, so that hypothalamus and pituitary gland may be regarded as a functional unit." fields.label: Diabetes insipidus
fields.definition: "A state of excessive water intake and hypotonic (dilute) polyuria. Histologically, the papules are characterized by superficial dilated capillaries in papillary dermis with epidermal proliferation." []

fields.label: Cigarette-paper scars
fields.definition: "Thin (atrophic) and wide scars." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Cigarette paper scarring; Cigarette-paper scars

fields.label: Atypical nevi in non-sun exposed areas

fields.label: Atrophic scars
fields.definition: "Scars that form a depression compared to the level of the surrounding skin because of damage to the collagen, fat or other tissues below the skin." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
synonyms: Sunken or indented skin due to damage

fields.label: Glabellar hemangioma

fields.label: Biliary tract abnormality
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the biliary tree." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Biliary tract disease

fields.label: Cholelithiasis
fields.definition: "Hard, pebble-like deposits that form within the gallbladder." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Cholecystitis

fields.synonyms_concat: Gallbladder inflammation

fields.label: Ectopia lentis
fields.definition: "Dislocation or malposition of the crystalline lens of the eye. A partial displacement (or dislocation) of the lens is described as a subluxation of the lens, while a complete displacement is termed luxation of the lens. A complete displacement occurs if the lens is completely outside the patellar fossa of the lens, either in the anterior chamber, in the vitreous, or directly on the retina. If the lens is partially displaced but still contained within the lens space, then it is termed subluxation." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of lens position; Lens dislocation

fields.label: Corneal arcus
fields.definition: "A hazy, grayish-white ring about 2 mm in width located close to but separated from the limbus (the corneoscleral junction). Corneal arcus generally occurs bilaterally, and is related to lipid deposition in the cornea. Corneal arcus can occur in elderly persons as a part of the aging process but may be associated with hypercholesterolemia in people under the age of 50 years." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Anterior embryotoxon; Arcus juvenilis; Arcus lipoidis; Arcus senilis; Corneal annulus; Gerontoxon

fields.label: Papilledema

fields.synonyms_concat: Papillitis

fields.label: Developmental glaucoma
fields.definition: "Glaucoma which forms during the early years of a child's life is called developmental or congenital glaucoma." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Childhood glaucoma; Infantile glaucoma; Paediatric glaucoma; Pediatric glaucoma

fields.label: Brushfield spots
fields.definition: "The presence of whitish spots in a ring-like arrangement at the periphery of the iris." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Iris brushfield spots; Speckled iris

fields.label: Iris atrophy
fields.definition: "Loss of iris tissue (atrophy)" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Iris degeneration

fields.label: Abnormally large globe
fields.definition: "Diffusely large eye (with megalocornea) without glaucoma." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Increased size of eyes; Increased size of palpebral fissures; Large eyeballs; Large eyes; Large of palpebral fissures; Megalophthalmos

fields.label: Absent lacrimal punctum
fields.definition: "No identifiable superior and/or inferior lacrimal punctum." [PMID:19125427]

fields.label: Optic nerve dysplasia

fields.label: Iridocyclitis
fields.definition: "A type of anterior uveitis, in which there is Inflammation of the iris and the ciliary body." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Hypertensive retinopathy
fields.definition: "Condition of the retina, secondary to severe systemic arterial hypertension which can be acute or longstanding. Features include one or several of the following: retinal vascular tortuosity, arteriovenous crossing signs, retinal cotton wool spot and intraretinal hemorrhages. It can be associated with optic disc swelling." [PMID:36196693]

fields.label: Keratoconjunctivitis
fields.definition: "Inflammation of the cornea and conjunctiva." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Keratoconjunctivitis sicca
fields.definition: "Dryness of the eye related to deficiency of the tear film components (aqueous, mucin, or lipid), lid surface abnormalities, or epithelial abnormalities. Keratoconjunctivitis sicca often results in a scratchy or sandy sensation (foreign body sensation) in the eyes, and may also be associated with itching, inability to produce tears, photosensitivity, redness, pain, and difficulty in moving the eyelids." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Dry eye syndrome; Dry eyes; Keratitis sicca; Xerophthalmia

fields.label: Abnormal fundus morphology
fields.definition: "Any structural abnormality of the fundus of the eye." []

fields.label: Atrophic fundus lesion
fields.definition: "Well-defined or diffused area or lesion of loss of normal retinal tissue; this is often illustrated by greyish discoloration of fundus and/or better visible choroidal vasculature on funduscopy." []

fields.label: Heterochromia iridis
fields.definition: "Heterochromia iridis is a difference in the color of the iris in the two eyes." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Different colored eyes; Different coloured eyes; Heterochromia irides

fields.label: Iritis
fields.definition: "Inflammation of the iris." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Inflammation of iris

fields.label: Angioid streaks
fields.definition: "Irregular lines in the outer retina and Bruch membrane that are typically configured in a radiating fashion and emanate from the optic disc. Angioid streaks are crack-like dehiscences in abnormally thickened and calcified Bruch membrane, resulting in atrophy of the overlying retinal pigment epithelium. They may be associated with a number of endocrine, metabolic, and connective tissue abnormalities but can be idiopathic. They can be associated with neovascular complexes (choroid)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123, PMID:30844178]
fields.synonyms_concat: Angioid streaks of the fundus; Angioid streaks of the retina; Angioid streaks, retina; Knapp streaks; Laquer cracks of the retina

fields.label: Abnormal macular morphology
fields.definition: "A structural abnormality of the macula, a region that, in a clinical context, is typically used to describe the central part of the retina within the vascular arcades." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:16255686]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the macula; Macula abnormality; Macular abnormality

fields.label: Macular hypoplasia

fields.label: Retinal atrophy
fields.definition: "A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and neurosensory retinal cells." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123]

fields.label: Periorbital hyperpigmentation

fields.synonyms_concat: Absent pigmentation in the eye; Albinism, Ocular

fields.label: Leber optic atrophy
fields.definition: "Degeneration of retinal ganglion cells and their axons." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Leber optic atrophy features; Leber optic degeneration

fields.label: Xanthelasma
fields.definition: "The presence of xanthomata in the skin of the eyelid." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.synonyms_concat: Fatty deposits in skin around the eyes; Fatty deposits on eyelids; Xanthelasma of eyelid; Xanthelasma of periocular region; Xanthelasma palpebrarum; Xanthoma; Xanthoma of eyelid; Xanthoma of periocular region

fields.label: Posterior polar cataract
fields.definition: "A polar cataract that affects the posterior pole of the lens." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Polar cataract, posterior

fields.label: Macular pseudocoloboma

fields.synonyms_concat: Coloboma of the macula; Macular coloboma

fields.label: Sudden loss of visual acuity

fields.synonyms_concat: Sudden central visual loss; Sudden decrease in vision

fields.definition: "A type of cataract that is not apparent at birth but that arises in childhood or adolescence." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Keratoglobus

fields.label: Abnormality of corneal size

fields.definition: "Cryptophthalmos is a condition of total absence of eyelids and the skin of forehead is continuous with that of cheek, in which the eyeball is completely concealed by the skin, which is stretched over the orbital cavity." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:19125427]

fields.label: Trichiasis

fields.synonyms_concat: Ingrown eyelashes; Introversion of eyelashes; Trichiasis of eyelid eyelashes

fields.label: Large central visual field defect
synonyms: Large central loss of field of vision
fields.synonyms_concat: Large central loss of field of vision

fields.label: Corneal dystrophy
fields.definition: "The term corneal dystrophy embraces a heterogenous group of bilateral genetically determined non-inflammatory corneal diseases that are restricted to the cornea." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Lens subluxation
fields.definition: "Partial dislocation of the lens of the eye." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Partially dislocated lens

fields.label: Constriction of peripheral visual field
fields.definition: "An absolute or relative decrease in retinal sensitivity extending from edge (periphery) of the visual field in a concentric pattern. The visual field is the area that is perceived simultaneously by a fixating eye." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123]
fields.synonyms_concat: Concentric narrowing of visual field; Constricted visual field; Constricted visual fields; Limited peripheral vision; Reduced peripheral vision; Visual field constriction

fields.label: Anterior polar cataract
fields.definition: "A polar cataract that affects the anterior pole of the lens." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Polar cataract, anterior

fields.label: Retinal arteriolar tortuosity

fields.synonyms_concat: Alternating cross eyes

fields.definition: "A benign tumor typically found at the junction of the cornea and sclera (limbal epibullar dermoid)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Benign eye tumor; Benign eye tumour; Epibulbar dermoid; Epibulbar dermoids

fields.label: Severely reduced visual acuity
fields.definition: "Severe reduction of the ability to see. On the 6m visual acuity scale, severe reduction is defined as less than 6/60 but at least 3/60. On the 20ft visual acuity scale, severe reduction is defined as less than 20/200 but at least 20/400. fields.label: Orbital cyst
fields.definition: "Presence of a cyst in the region of the periorbital tissues. fields.synonyms_concat: Cyst of eye socket; Orbital cysts

fields.label: Lattice corneal dystrophy
fields.definition: "The presence of fine, branching linear opacities in Bowman's layer in the central area that may spread to the periphery in the clinical course. fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal horizontal ocular pursuit; Impaired horizontal visual pursuit

fields.definition: "An abnormality of tracking eye movements in which smooth pursuit is interrupted by an abnormally high number of saccadic movements." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Saccadic pursuit movements; Saccadic slow pursuit; Saccadic smooth pursuit

fields.label: Septate vagina

fields.synonyms_concat: Double vagina

fields.label: Abnormality of the hand

fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal hands; Abnormality of the hand; Hand anomalies; Hand deformities

fields.synonyms_concat: Brachydactyly syndrome; Short fingers or toes

fields.label: Syndactyly
fields.definition: "Webbing or fusion of the fingers or toes, involving soft parts only or including bone structure. Bony fusions are referred to as \"bony\" syndactyly if the fusion occurs in a radio-ulnar axis. Fusions of bones of the fingers or toes in a proximo-distal axis are referred to as \"symphalangism\"." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Webbed fingers or toes

fields.label: Hand polydactyly
fields.definition: "A kind of polydactyly characterized by the presence of a supernumerary finger or fingers." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Abnormal finger morphology

fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormalities of the fingers; Abnormality of finger

fields.label: Broad palm

[https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Broad hand; Broad hands; Broad palm; Wide palm

fields.label: Split hand
fields.definition: "A condition in which middle parts of the hand (fingers and metacarpals) are missing giving a cleft appearance. The severity is very variable ranging from slightly hypoplastic middle fingers over absent middle fingers as far as oligo- or monodactyl hands." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Ectrodactyly of the hand; Hand ectrodactyly; Split hand; Split-hand

fields.label: Abnormal thumb morphology
fields.definition: "An abnormal structure of the first digit of the hand." []

fields.label: Large hands

fields.definition: "Supernumerary digits located at the radial side of the hand. Polydactyly (supernumerary digits) involving the thumb occurs in many distinct forms of high variability and severity. Ranging from fleshy nubbins over varying degrees of partial duplication/splitting to completely duplicated or even triplicated thumbs or preaxial (on the radial side of the hand) supernumerary digits." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Extra thumb; Polydactyly affecting the thumb; Preaxial polydactyly of hands; Supernumerary thumb; thumb polydactyly

fields.label: Adducted thumb
fields.definition: "In the resting position, the tip of the thumb is on, or near, the palm, close to the base of the fourth or fifth finger." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6670-9157, PMID:16235349, PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Adducted thumbs; Inward turned thumb; Thumb-in-palm deformity; Thumb-in-palm pattern

fields.label: Tapered finger
fields.definition: "The gradual reduction in girth of the finger from proximal to distal." [PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Distally tapering fingers; Tapered finger; Tapered fingers; Tapered fingertips; Tapering fingers

fields.label: Hyperextensibility of the finger joints
fields.definition: "The ability of the finger joints to move beyond their normal range of motion." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Finger joint hyperextensibility; Hyperextensible digits; Hyperextensible finger; Hyperextensible fingers

fields.label: Hand clenching
fields.definition: "An abnormal hand posture in which the hands are clenched to fists. All digits held completely flexed at the metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints. In prenatal sonography of the fetal clenched hand, the index finger overlaps a clenched fist formed by the other digits. The proximal interphalangeal articulation of the index finger is flexed and ulnarly deviated, and the thumb is adducted." fields.synonyms_concat: Clenched hand; Clenched hands; Fisted hand; Fisting; Hand clenching; Hands fisted; Hands tightly fisted; Thumb clasp

fields.synonyms_concat: Short umbilical cord

fields.label: Abnormality of prenatal development or birth
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the fetus or the birth of the fetus, excluding structural abnormalities." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Prominent fingertip pads

The basal ganglia and brainstem nuclei could be shown to have a yellow staining historically in infants who died of kernicterus, that is, kernicterus is strictly speaking a pathological diagnosis. The presence of kernicterus may be inferred in infants with characteristic acute or chronic bilirubin-induced neurological dysfunction." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Rotary nystagmus

fields.synonyms_concat: Rotatory Nystagmus

fields.synonyms_concat: Bell-shaped chest; Constricted, bell-shaped thorax; Narrow, bell-shaped thorax

fields.label: Abnormal hair morphology

fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the hair; Abnormality of the hair shaft; Hair abnormality

fields.label: Alopecia

fields.synonyms_concat: Hair loss

fields.label: Abnormal nail morphology

fields.synonyms_concat: Laryngeal abnormalities; Laryngeal anomalies

fields.definition: "Laryngomalacia is a congenital abnormality of the laryngeal cartilage in which the cartilage is floppy and prolapses over the larynx during inspiration." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Softening of voice box tissue

fields.label: Vocal cord paresis
fields.definition: "Decreased strength of the vocal folds." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

Vocal cord paresis in severe cases
fields.synonyms_concat: Hoarse voice due to vocal cord paresis; Vocal cord paresis in severe cases; Weakness of the vocal cords

fields.label: Vocal cord paralysis
fields.definition: "A loss of the ability to move the vocal folds." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Inability to move vocal cords; Laryngeal paralysis

fields.label: Abnormality of the voice
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the voice; Voice abnormality

fields.label: Hoarse voice
fields.definition: "Hoarseness refers to a change in the pitch or quality of the voice, with the voice sounding weak, very breathy, scratchy, or husky." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Hoarse voice; Hoarseness; Husky voice

fields.definition: "A type of speech characterized by the presence of an abnormally increased nasal airflow during speech associated with structural abnormality of the nasal passages." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Hypernasal voice; Nasal speech; Nasal voice

fields.label: Hoarse cry
fields.synonyms_concat: Hoarse cry

fields.label: Dysphonia
fields.definition: "Difficulty in speaking due to a physical disorder of the mouth, tongue, throat, or vocal cords. Associated with a known physical or neurological cause." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Inability to produce voice sounds; Voice change

fields.label: Abnormally high-pitched voice
fields.definition: "A persistent (minutes to hours) abnormal increase in the pitch (frequency) of the voice for the context or social situation or significantly different from baseline of the individual." []
fields.synonyms_concat: High pitched voice; High-pitched voice

fields.label: Weak voice
fields.definition: "Reduced intensity (volume) of speech." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Hypophonia; Quiet voice; Soft voice; Weak voice

fields.label: Premature birth
fields.definition: "The birth of a baby of less than 37 weeks of gestational age." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Premature birth; Premature delivery; Premature delivery of affected infants; Preterm birth; Preterm delivery; Shortened gestation time

fields.label: Breech presentation

Feet or buttocks of foetus positioned near opening of uterus

fields.label: Abnormal heart morphology
fields.definition: "Any structural anomaly of the heart." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Ventricular septal defect
fields.definition: "A hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart. The defect is centered around the most superior aspect of the ventricular septum." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:33327983]
synonyms: Hole in heart wall separating two lower heart chambers

fields.label: Atrial septal defect
fields.definition: "Atrial septal defect (ASD) is a congenital abnormality of the interatrial septum that enables blood flow between the left and right atria via the interatrial septum." [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
synonyms: An opening in the wall separating the top two chambers of the heart
Hole in heart wall separating two upper heart chambers
fields.synonyms_concat: An opening in the wall separating the top two chambers of the heart; ASD; Atria septal defect; Atrial septum defect; Atrioseptal defect; Defect in the atrial septum; Hole in heart wall separating two upper heart chambers

fields.label: Abnormal mitral valve morphology
fields.definition: "Any structural anomaly of the mitral valve." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the mitral valve

fields.label: Mitral valve prolapse
fields.definition: "One or both of the leaflets (cusps) of the mitral valve bulges back into the left atrium upon contraction of the left ventricle." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Congestive heart failure
fields.definition: "The presence of an abnormality of cardiac function that is responsible for the failure of the heart to pump blood at a rate that is commensurate with the needs of the tissues or a state in which abnormally elevated filling pressures are required for the heart to do so. Heart failure is frequently related to a defect in myocardial contraction." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Cardiac failure; Cardiac failures; Cardiac insufficiency; CHF; Chronic heart failure; Heart failure

fields.label: Tetralogy of Fallot
fields.definition: "A congenital cardiac malformation comprising pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta, ventricular septum defect, and right ventricular hypertrophy. The diagnosis of TOF is made if at least three of the four above mentioned features are present." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Tetrology of fallot

fields.label: Abnormal myocardium morphology
fields.definition: "A structural anomaly of the muscle layer of the heart wall." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the myocardium

fields.label: Cardiomyopathy
fields.definition: "A myocardial disorder in which the heart muscle is structurally and functionally abnormal, in the absence of coronary artery disease, hypertension, valvular disease and congenital heart disease sufficient to cause the observed myocardial abnormality." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:17916581]
fields.synonyms_concat: Disease of the heart muscle

fields.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
fields.definition: "Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is defined by the presence of increased ventricular wall thickness or mass in the absence of loading conditions (hypertension, valve disease) sufficient to cause the observed abnormality." [PMID:17916581]
fields.synonyms_concat: Cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic; Enlarged and thickened heart muscle; HCM

fields.label: Cardiomegaly
fields.definition: "Increased size of the heart, clinically defined as an increased transverse diameter of the cardiac silhouette that is greater than or equal to 50% of the transverse diameter of the chest (increased cardiothoracic ratio) on a posterior-anterior projection of a chest radiograph or a computed tomography." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:31194436]
fields.synonyms_concat: Enlarged heart; Increased heart size

fields.label: Abnormal pulmonary valve morphology
fields.definition: "Any structural abnormality of the pulmonary valve." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the pulmonary valve; Anomaly of the pulmonary valve

fields.label: Pulmonic stenosis
fields.definition: "A narrowing of the right ventricular outflow tract that can occur at the pulmonary valve (valvular stenosis), below the pulmonary valve (infundibular stenosis), or above the pulmonary valve (supravalvar stenosis)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Narrowing of pulmonic valve; Pulmonary stenosis; Pulmonary valve stenosis; Pulmonic valve stenosis

fields.label: Patent ductus arteriosus
fields.definition: "In utero, the ductus arteriosus (DA) serves to divert ventricular output away from the lungs and toward the placenta by connecting the main pulmonary artery to the descending aorta. A patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in the first 3 days of life is a physiologic shunt in healthy term and preterm newborn infants, and normally is substantially closed within about 24 hours after bith and completely closed after about three weeks. Failure of physiologcal closure is referred to a persistent or patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). Depending on the degree of left-to-right shunting, PDA can have clinical consequences." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:20421261]
fields.synonyms_concat: Ductus arteriosus; Patent ductus Botalli; PDA; Persistent arterial duct; Persistent ductus arteriosus

fields.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
fields.definition: "Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is defined by the presence of left ventricular dilatation and left ventricular systolic dysfunction in the absence of abnormal loading conditions (hypertension, valve disease) or coronary artery disease sufficient to cause global systolic impairment. Right ventricular dilation and dysfunction may be present but are not necessary for the diagnosis." [PMID:17916581]
fields.synonyms_concat: Cardiomyopathy, dilated; Congestive cardiomyopathy; DCM; Stretched and thinned heart muscle

fields.label: Sudden cardiac death
fields.definition: "The heart suddenly and unexpectedly stops beating resulting in death within a short time period (generally within 1 h of symptom onset)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Premature sudden cardiac death; Sudden cardiac death

fields.label: Abnormal aortic valve morphology
fields.definition: "Any abnormality of the aortic valve." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the aortic valve

fields.label: Bicuspid aortic valve
fields.definition: "The presence of an aortic valve with two instead of the normal three cusps (flaps). Bicuspid aortic valvue is a malformation of a commissure (small space between the attachment of each cusp to the aortic wall) and the adjacent parts of the two corresponding cusps forming a raphe (the fused area of the two underdeveloped cusps turning into a malformed commissure between both cusps; the raphe is a fibrous ridge that extends from the commissure to the free edge of the two underdeveloped, conjoint cusps)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:17467434, PMID:24827036]
synonyms: Aortic valve has two leaflets rather than three
fields.synonyms_concat: Aortic valve has two leaflets rather than three

fields.label: Cor pulmonale
fields.definition: "Right-sided heart failure resulting from chronic hypertension in the pulmonary arteries and right ventricle." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Tachycardia
fields.definition: "A rapid heartrate that exceeds the range of the normal resting heartrate for age." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Elevated heart rate; Fast heart rate; Heart racing; Increased heart rate; Racing heart; Rapid heart beat

fields.label: Aortic valve stenosis
fields.definition: "The presence of a stenosis (narrowing) of the aortic valve." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Aortic stenosis; Narrowing of aortic valve; Valvular aortic stenosis

fields.label: Dextrocardia
fields.definition: "The heart is located in the right hand sided hemithorax. That is, there is a left-right reversal (or \"mirror reflection\") of the anatomical location of the heart in which the heart is locate on the right side instead of the left." [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
synonyms: Heart tip and four chambers point towards right side of body
fields.synonyms_concat: Heart tip and four chambers point towards right side of body; Thoracic situs inversus

fields.label: Mitral regurgitation
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the mitral valve characterized by insufficiency or incompetence of the mitral valve resulting in retrograde leaking of blood through the mitral valve upon ventricular contraction." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Mitral incompetence; Mitral insufficiency; Mitral regurgitation, mild; Mitral valve insufficiency; Mitral valve regurgitation

fields.label: Abnormal heart valve morphology
fields.definition: "Any structural abnormality of a cardiac valve." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the heart valves; Valvular abnormality; Valvular heart disease

fields.label: Patent foramen ovale
fields.definition: "Failure of the foramen ovale to seal postnatally, leaving a potential conduit between the left and right cardiac atria." [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Persistent foramen ovale; PFO

fields.label: Prolonged QT interval
fields.definition: "Increased time between the start of the Q wave and the end of the T wave as measured by the electrocardiogram (EKG)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Long Q-T syndrome; Long QT syndrome; Prolong qt interval on ekg

fields.label: Myocardial infarction
fields.definition: "Necrosis of the myocardium caused by an obstruction of the blood supply to the heart and often associated with chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, and anxiety as well as characteristic EKG findings and elevation of serum markers including creatine kinase-MB fraction and troponin." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Heart attack; MI

fields.label: Aortic regurgitation
fields.definition: "An insufficiency of the aortic valve, leading to regurgitation (backward flow) of blood from the aorta into the left ventricle." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Aortic insufficiency; Aortic valve regurgitation

fields.label: Truncus arteriosus
fields.definition: "A single arterial trunk arises from the cardiac mass. The pulmonary arteries, aorta and coronary arteries arise from this single trunk with no evidence of another outflow tract." [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Common arterial trunk; Persistent truncus arteriosus

fields.label: Bradycardia
fields.definition: "A slower than normal heart rate (in adults, slower than 60 beats per minute)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Brachycardia; Slow heartbeats

fields.label: Ventricular fibrillation
fields.definition: "Uncontrolled contractions of muscles fibers in the left ventricle not producing contraction of the left ventricle. Ventricular fibrillation usually begins with a ventricular premature contraction and a short run of rapid ventricular tachycardia degenerating into uncoordinating ventricular fibrillations." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Torsade de pointes
fields.definition: "A type of ventricular tachycardia characterized by polymorphioc QRS complexes that change in amplitue and cycle length, and thus have the appearance of oscillating around the baseline in the EKG." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Torsades de pointes

fields.label: Right ventricular hypertrophy
fields.definition: "In this case the right ventricle is more muscular than normal, causing a characteristic boot-shaped (coeur-en-sabot) appearance as seen on anterior- posterior chest x-rays. Right ventricular hypertrophy is commonly associated with any form of right ventricular outflow obstruction or pulmonary hypertension, which may in turn owe its origin to left-sided disease. The echocardiographic signs are thickening of the anterior right ventricular wall and the septum. Cavity size is usually normal, or slightly enlarged. In many cases there is associated volume overload present due to tricuspid regurgitation, in the absence of this, septal motion is normal." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Heart right ventricle hypertrophy

fields.label: Transposition of the great arteries
fields.definition: "A complex congenital heart defect in which the aorta arises from the morphologic right ventricle and the pulmonary artery arises from the morphologic left ventricle." [eMedicine:900574, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:10798431]
fields.synonyms_concat: TGA; TGV; Transposition of great vessels

fields.label: Asymmetric septal hypertrophy
fields.definition: "Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with an asymmetrical pattern of hypertrophy, with a predilection for the interventricular septum and myocyte disarray." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:17916581]

fields.label: Abnormal cardiac septum morphology
fields.definition: "An anomaly of the intra-atrial or intraventricular septum." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the cardiac septa; Heart septal defect; Septal defects

fields.label: Complete atrioventricular canal defect
fields.definition: "A congenital heart defect characterized by a specific combination of heart defects with a common atrioventricular valve, primum atrial septal defect and inlet ventricular septal defect." [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:16722604]
fields.synonyms_concat: Common atrioventricular canal; Complete atrioventricular canal; Complete atrioventricular septal defect; Complete common AV canal

fields.label: Coronary artery atherosclerosis
fields.definition: "Reduction of the diameter of the coronary arteries as the result of an accumulation of atheromatous plaques within the walls of the coronary arteries, which increases the risk of myocardial ischemia." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:31420554]
synonyms: Plaque build-up in arteries supplying blood to heart
fields.synonyms_concat: Coronary atherosclerosis; Coronary disease; Plaque build-up in arteries supplying blood to heart

fields.label: Atrioventricular block
fields.definition: "Delayed or lack of conduction of atrial depolarizations through the atrioventricular node to the ventricles." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
synonyms: Interruption of electrical communication between upper and lower chambers of heart
fields.synonyms_concat: Atrioventricular nodal disease; Interruption of electrical communication between upper and lower chambers of heart

fields.label: Abnormal aortic morphology
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the aorta." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:24910511]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal aorta morphology; Abnormality of the aorta

fields.label: Coarctation of aorta
fields.definition: "Coarctation of the aorta is a narrowing or constriction of a segment of the aorta." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:23909637]
fields.synonyms_concat: Aortic coarctation; Coarctation of the aorta; Narrowing of aorta; Narrowing of the aorta

fields.label: Angina pectoris
fields.definition: "Paroxysmal chest pain that occurs with exertion or stress and is related to myocardial ischemia." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Subvalvular aortic stenosis
fields.definition: "A fixed form of obstruction to blood flow across the left-ventricular outflow tract related to stenosis (narrowing) below the level of the aortic valve." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
synonyms: Narrowing of blood vessel below aortic heart valve
fields.synonyms_concat: Narrowing of blood vessel below aortic heart valve; Subaortic stenosis

fields.label: Ectopia cordis
fields.definition: "Congenital malformation of the ventral wall with partial or total evisceration of the heart outside the thoracic cavity and through the defect in the ventral wall." [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]

fields.label: Secundum atrial septal defect
fields.definition: "A kind of atrial septum defect arising from an enlarged foramen ovale, inadequate growth of the septum secundum, or excessive absorption of the septum primum." [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
synonyms: Atrial septal defect, ostium secundum type
fields.synonyms_concat: Atrial septal defect, ostium secundum type; Ostium secundum atrial septal defect; Patent ostium secundum

fields.label: Myocardial fibrosis
fields.definition: "Myocardial fibrosis is characterized by dysregulated collagen turnover (increased synthesis predominates over unchanged or decreased degradation) and excessive diffuse collagen accumulation in the interstitial and perivascular spaces as well as by phenotypically transformed fibroblasts, termed myofibroblasts." [PMID:28157267]

fields.label: Loss of voice
fields.synonyms_concat: Aphonia

fields.label: Sinus bradycardia
fields.definition: "Bradycardia related to a mean resting sinus rate of less than 50 beats per minute." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Muscular subvalvular aortic stenosis
fields.definition: "A type of subvalvular aortic stenosis resulting from thickening of the musculature of the interventricular septum, which results in obstruction to blood flow through the left-ventricular outflow tract." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Muscular subaortic stenosis

fields.label: Atrial arrhythmia
fields.definition: "A type of supraventricular tachycardia in which the atria are the principal site of electrophysiologic disturbance." [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]
fields.synonyms_concat: Primary atrial arrhythmia

fields.label: Cardiac shunt
fields.definition: "Pattern of blood flow in the heart that deviates from the normal circuit of the circulatory system." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Right-to-left shunt
fields.definition: "Pattern of blood flow in the heart that deviates from the normal circuit of the circulatory system from the right side of the heart to the left." [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9114-8737]

fields.label: Cardiac arrest
fields.definition: "An abrupt loss of heart function." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Heart stops beating

fields.label: Situs inversus totalis
fields.definition: "A left-right reversal (or mirror reflection) of the anatomical location of the major thoracic and abdominal organs." [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
synonyms: All organs on wrong side of body
fields.synonyms_concat: All organs on wrong side of body; Situs inversus; situs oppositus; situs transversus

fields.label: Abnormal pericardium morphology
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the pericardium, i.e., of the fluid filled sac that surrounds the heart and the proximal ends of the aorta, vena cava, and the pulmonary artery." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the pericardium

fields.label: Pericardial effusion
fields.definition: "Accumulation of fluid within the pericardium." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Fluid around heart; Pericardial effusions

fields.label: Sudden death
fields.definition: "Rapid and unexpected death." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Myocardial necrosis
fields.definition: "Irreversible damage to heart tissue (myocardium) due to lack of oxygen after a heart attack (myocardial infarction)." [PMID:20405318]

fields.label: Pericarditis
fields.definition: "Inflammation of the sac-like covering around the heart (pericardium)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
synonyms: Swelling or irritation of membrane around heart
fields.synonyms_concat: Swelling or irritation of membrane around heart

fields.label: Abnormal tricuspid valve morphology
fields.definition: "Any structural anomaly of the tricuspid valve." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the tricuspid valve

fields.label: Tricuspid valve prolapse
fields.definition: "One or more of the leaflets (cusps) of the tricuspid valve bulges back into the right atrium upon contraction of the right ventricle." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Right ventricular outlet tract obstruction
fields.definition: "An obstruction to the forward flow of blood in the outflow tract of the right ventricle." [PMID:30038501]
fields.synonyms_concat: Right ventricular outlet obstruction

fields.label: Endocardial fibroelastosis
fields.definition: "Diffuse thickening of the ventricular endocardium and by associated myocardial dysfunction" [PMID:23109776]

fields.label: Abnormal right ventricle morphology
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the right ventricle of the heart." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the right ventricle; Right ventricular abnormality

fields.label: Right ventricular failure
fields.definition: "Reduced ability of the right ventricle to perform its function (to receive blood from the right atrium and to eject blood into the pulmonary artery), often leading to pitting peripheral edema, ascites, and hepatomegaly." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Impaired right ventricular function; Right ventricular impairment; Right-sided heart failure

fields.label: Third degree atrioventricular block
fields.definition: "Third-degree atrioventricular (AV) block (also referred to as complete heart block) is the complete dissociation of the atria and the ventricles. Third-degree AV block exists when more P waves than QRS complexes exist and no relationship (no conduction) exists between them." [PMID:21841933]
fields.synonyms_concat: Complete heart block; Third-degree heart block

fields.label: Conotruncal defect
fields.definition: "A congenital malformation of the outflow tract of the heart. Conotruncal defects are thought to result from a disturbance of the outflow tract of the embryonic heart, and comprise truncus arteriosus, tetralogy of Fallot, interrupted aortic arch, transposition of the great arteries, and double outlet right ventricle." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Conotruncal heart defects

fields.label: Abnormal left ventricle morphology
fields.definition: "Any structural abnormality of the left ventricle of the heart." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal heart left ventricle morphology; Abnormality of the left ventricle; Left ventricular abnormality

fields.label: Left ventricular hypertrophy
fields.definition: "Enlargement or increased size of the heart left ventricle." [MP:0002625]
fields.synonyms_concat: Heart left ventricle hypertrophy; Left ventricular wall hypertrophy

fields.label: Abnormal cardiac ventricle morphology
fields.definition: "An abnormality of a cardiac ventricle." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of cardiac ventricle

fields.label: Ventricular hypertrophy
fields.definition: "Enlargement of the cardiac ventricular muscle tissue with increase in the width of the wall of the ventricle and loss of elasticity. Ventricular hypertrophy is clinically differentiated into left and right ventricular hypertrophy." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
fields.definition: "A disorder of the cardiac conduction system of the heart characterized by ventricular preexcitation due to the presence of an abnormal accessory atrioventricular electrical conduction pathway." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Coronary artery calcification
fields.definition: "An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in a coronary artery." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Mitral stenosis
fields.definition: "An abnormal narrowing of the orifice of the mitral valve." [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown]
fields.synonyms_concat: Mitral valve stenosis

fields.label: Double outlet right ventricle
fields.definition: "Double outlet right ventricle (DORV) is a type of ventriculoarterial connection in which both great vessels arise entirely or predominantly from the right ventricle." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:10798433]
fields.synonyms_concat: DORV; Double-outlet right ventricle

fields.label: High-output congestive heart failure
fields.definition: "A form of heart failure characterized by elevated cardiac output. This may be seen in patients with heart failure and hyperthyroidism, anemia, pregnancy, arteriovenous fistulae, and others." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
fields.definition: "Restrictive left ventricular physiology is characterized by a pattern of ventricular filling in which increased stiffness of the myocardium causes ventricular pressure to rise precipitously with only small increases in volume, defined as restrictive ventricular physiology in the presence of normal or reduced diastolic volumes (of one or both ventricles), normal or reduced systolic volumes, and normal ventricular wall thickness." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:17916581]

fields.label: Thromboembolic stroke
fields.definition: "A cerebrovascular accident (stroke) that occurs because of thromboembolism." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Progressive hearing impairment
fields.definition: "A progressive form of hearing impairment." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Progressive hearing loss

fields.label: Abnormality of the pancreas
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the pancreas." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the pancreas; Pancreatic disease

fields.label: Pancreatitis
fields.definition: "The presence of inflammation in the pancreas." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Pancreatic inflammation

fields.label: Annular pancreas
fields.definition: "A congenital anomaly in which the pancreas completely (or sometimes incompletely) encircles the second portion of duodenum and occasionally obstructs the more proximal duodenum." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Acute pancreatitis
fields.definition: "A acute form of pancreatitis." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Acute pancreatic inflammation; Pancreatitis, acute

fields.label: Pancreatic cysts
fields.definition: "A cyst of the pancreas that possess a lining of mucous epithelium." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Multiple pancreatic cysts; Pancreatic cyst; Pancreatic cysts

fields.label: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
fields.definition: "Impaired function of the exocrine pancreas associated with a reduced ability to digest foods because of lack of digestive enzymes." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
synonyms: Inability to properly digest food due to lack of pancreatic digestive enzymes
fields.synonyms_concat: Inability to properly digest food due to lack of pancreatic digestive enzymes; Pancreatic insufficiency

fields.label: Abnormal nasopharynx morphology
fields.definition: "A structural anomaly of the nasopharynx." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the nasopharynx

fields.label: Phimosis
fields.definition: "The male foreskin cannot be fully retracted from the head of the penis." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Nasal congestion
fields.definition: "Reduced ability to pass air through the nasal cavity often leading to mouth breathing." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Blockage of nose; Congestion of nose; Nasal blockage; Nasal obstruction; Obstruction of nose; Stuffy nose

fields.label: Abnormality of the spleen
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the spleen." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of the spleen

fields.label: Splenomegaly
fields.definition: "Abnormal increased size of the spleen." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Increased spleen size; Large spleen

fields.label: Asplenia
fields.definition: "Absence (aplasia) of the spleen." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Absent spleen

fields.label: Accessory spleen
fields.definition: "An accessory spleen is a round, iso-echogenic, homogenic and smooth structure and is seen as a normal variant mostly on the medial contour of the spleen, near the hilus or around the lower pole. This has no pathogenic relevance." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Polysplenia
fields.definition: "Polysplenia is a congenital disease manifested by multiple small accessory spleens." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Accessory spleens; Multiple accessory spleens; Multiple small spleens

fields.label: Single ventricle
fields.definition: "The presence of only one working lower chamber in the heart, usually with a virtual absence of the ventricular septum and usually present in conjunction with double inlet left or right ventricle." [MP:0010432]
fields.synonyms_concat: Common ventricle

fields.label: Abnormal vestibular function
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the functioning of the vestibular apparatus." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Impaired vestibular function; Interictal vestibular dysfunction; Vestibular function defect

fields.label: Vestibular hyporeflexia
fields.definition: "A general descriptive term that describes impaired functioning of the vestibular apparatus that leads to manifestations such as dizziness or postural imbalance" [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:32767115]
fields.synonyms_concat: Vestibular deficiency; Vestibular dysfunction; Vestibular failure; Vestibular hypofunction; Vestibular hyporeflexia; Vestibular loss; Vestibulopathy

fields.label: High-frequency sensorineural hearing impairment
fields.definition: "A form of sensorineural hearing impairment that affects primarily the higher frequencies." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: High frequency sensorineural hearing impairment; High-tone sensorineural deafness; High-tone sensorineural hearing impairment

fields.label: Abnormal foot morphology
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the skeleton of foot." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal feet structure; Abnormality of the feet; Abnormality of the foot; Foot deformities; Foot deformity

fields.label: Pes cavus
fields.definition: "An increase in height of the medial longitudinal arch of the foot that does not flatten on weight bearing (i.e., a distinctly hollow form of the sole of the foot when it is bearing weight)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Cavus foot; High-arched foot

fields.label: Talipes equinovarus
fields.definition: "Talipes equinovarus (also called clubfoot) typically has four main components: inversion and adduction of the forefoot; inversion of the heel and hindfoot; equinus (limitation of extension) of the ankle and subtalar joint; and internal rotation of the leg." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:32491773]
fields.synonyms_concat: Club feet; Club foot; Clubbing of feet; Clubfeet; Clubfoot; Equinovarus; Fetal foot inversion; Foetal foot inversion; Foot, talipes equinovarus; Pes equinovarus; Pes equinus

fields.label: Pes planus
fields.definition: "A foot where the longitudinal arch of the foot is in contact with the ground or floor when the individual is standing; or, in a patient lying supine, a foot where the arch is in contact with the surface of a flat board pressed against the sole of the foot by the examiner with a pressure similar to that expected from weight bearing; or, the height of the arch is reduced." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Dropped arches; Fallen arches; Flat feet; Flat foot

fields.label: Hammertoe
fields.definition: "Hyperextension of the metatarsal-phalangeal joint with hyperflexion of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint." [PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Hammer toe; Hammertoe; Hammertoes

fields.label: Broad foot
fields.definition: "A foot for which the measured width is above the 95th centile for age; or, a foot that appears disproportionately wide for its length." [PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Broad feet; Broad foot; Wide foot

fields.label: Toe syndactyly
fields.definition: "Webbing or fusion of the toes, involving soft parts only or including bone structure. Bony fusions are referred to as \"bony\" Syndactyly if the fusion occurs in a radio-ulnar axis. Fusions of bones of the toes in a proximo-distal axis are referred to as \"Symphalangism\"." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Foot syndactyly; Fused toes; Syndactyly of feet; Syndactyly of toes; Webbed toes

fields.label: Achilles tendon contracture
fields.definition: "A contracture of the Achilles tendon." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Achilles tendon contractures; Contractures of the Achilles tendon; Shortening of the achilles tendon; Tight achilles tendon

fields.label: Talipes equinovalgus
fields.definition: "A deformity of foot and ankle in which the foot is bent down and outwards." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Equinovalgus deformity

fields.label: Short foot
fields.definition: "A measured foot length that is more than 2 SD below the mean for a newborn of 27 - 41 weeks gestation, or foot that is less than the 3rd centile for individuals from birth to 16 years of age (objective). Alternatively, a foot that appears disproportionately short (subjective)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Hypoplastic feet; Short feet; Short foot; Small feet

fields.label: Bilateral talipes equinovarus
fields.definition: "Bilateral clubfoot deformity." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Bilateral clubfeet; Bilateral clubfoot; Club foot on both sides

fields.label: Abnormal toe morphology
fields.definition: "An anomaly of a toe." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormalities of the toes; Abnormality of toe

fields.label: Bulbous tips of toes
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the morphology of the toes, such that the tips of the toes are prominent and bulbous." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Broad metatarsal
fields.definition: "Increased side-to-side width of a metatarsal bone." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Broad metatarsals; Wide long bone of foot; Widened metatarsal shaft

fields.label: Ankle swelling
fields.synonyms_concat: Ankle swelling

fields.label: Narrow foot
fields.definition: "A foot for which the measured width is below the 5th centile for age; or, a foot that appears disproportionately narrow for its length." [PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Narrow foot; Slender feet

fields.label: Abnormal delivery
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the birth process." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal delivery; Delivery complication

fields.label: Premature rupture of membranes
fields.definition: "Premature rupture of membranes (PROM) is a condition which occurs in pregnancy when the amniotic sac ruptures more than an hour before the onset of labor." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Hydrops fetalis
fields.definition: "The abnormal accumulation of fluid in two or more fetal compartments, including ascites, pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, and skin edema." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Nonimmune hydrops fetalis
fields.definition: "A type of hydrops fetalis in which there is no identifiable circulating antibody to red blood cell antigens ." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Hydrops fetalis, non-immune; Hydrops fetalis, nonimmune; Non-immune fetal hydrops; Non-immune foetal hydrops; Nonimmune hydrops

fields.label: Fetal ascites
fields.definition: "Accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity during the fetal period." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Foetal ascites

fields.label: Small nail
fields.definition: "A nail that is diminished in length and width, i.e., underdeveloped nail." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Hypoplastic nail; Hypoplastic nails; Nail hypoplasia; Small nail; Small nails

fields.label: Hyperconvex nail
fields.definition: "When viewed on end (with the digit tip pointing toward the examiner's eye) the curve of the nail forms a tighter curve of convexity." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Increased nail curvature; Nail overcurvature

fields.label: Anonychia
fields.definition: "Aplasia of the nail." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Absent nails; Aplastic nails

fields.label: Short nail
fields.definition: "Decreased length of nail." [PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Short nail; Short nails

fields.label: Hypoplastic toenails
fields.definition: "Underdevelopment of the toenail." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Underdeveloped toenails

fields.label: Absent toenail
fields.definition: "Congenital absence of the toenail." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Absent toenail; Absent toenails; Absent toenails (anonychia); Anonychia of toenails

fields.label: Nail pits
fields.definition: "Small (typically about 1 mm or less in size) depressions on the dorsal nail surface." [PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Nail pits; Nail pitting; Pitted nails

fields.label: Hypoplastic fingernail
fields.definition: "Underdevelopment of a fingernail." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Small fingernail; Underdeveloped fingernail

fields.label: Onychogryphosis
fields.definition: "Onychogryphosis is a disorder of nail plate growth that is clinically characterized by an opaque, yellow-brown thickening of the nail plate with associated gross hyperkeratosis, elongation, and increased curvature." [PMID:19125433, PMID:30410908, PMID:33021642]
fields.synonyms_concat: Dystrophic thickened nails; Onychogryposis; Thick nail; Thickened nails

fields.label: Onycholysis
fields.definition: "Detachment of the nail from the nail bed." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Detachment of nail; Oncholysis

fields.label: Ridged nail
fields.definition: "Longitudinal, linear prominences in the nail plate." [PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Grooved nails; Longitudinal ridging; Nail ridging; Ridged nails

fields.label: Fragile nails
fields.definition: "Nails that easily break." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Brittle nails

fields.label: Split nail
fields.definition: "A nail plate that has a longitudinal separation and the two sections of the nail share the same lateral radius of curvature." [PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Longitudinal splitting of nail

fields.label: Dystrophic toenail
fields.definition: "Toenail changes apart from changes of the color of the toenail (nail dyschromia) that involve partial or complete disruption of the various keratinous layers of the nail plate." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Dystrophic toenail changes; Dystrophic toenails; Poor toenail formation

fields.label: Hyperconvex fingernails
fields.definition: "When viewed on end (with the finger tip pointing toward the examiner's eye) the curve of the fingernail forms a tighter curve of convexity." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Tubular fingernails

fields.label: Deep-set nails
fields.definition: "Deeply placed nails." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Deep-set nails

fields.label: Thin nail
fields.definition: "Nail that appears thin when viewed on end." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Thin nail; Thin nails

fields.label: Absent fingernail
fields.definition: "Absence of a fingernail." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Absent fingernail; Anonychia of fingernails; Aplasia of the fingernail

fields.label: Paronychia
fields.definition: "The nail disease paronychia is an often-tender bacterial or fungal hand infection or foot infection where the nail and skin meet at the side or the base of a finger or toenail. The infection can start suddenly (acute paronychia) or gradually (chronic paronychia)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Leukonychia
fields.definition: "White discoloration of the nails." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: White discoloration of nails

fields.label: Broad nail
fields.definition: "Increased width of nail." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Broad fingernails; Broad nail; Wide fingernails

fields.label: Hallux valgus
fields.definition: "Lateral deviation of the great toe (i.e., in the direction of the little toe)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Bunion; Lateral deviation of great toe; Lateral deviation of halluces

fields.label: Weight loss
fields.definition: "Reduction of total body weight." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Loss of weight

fields.label: Genital tract atresia
fields.definition: "Congenital occlusion of a tube in the genital tract." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Foot polydactyly
fields.definition: "A kind of polydactyly characterized by the presence of a supernumerary toe or toes." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
synonyms: Duplication of bones of the toes
fields.synonyms_concat: Duplication of bones of the toes; Polydactyly of feet; Polydactyly of the foot

fields.label: Postaxial foot polydactyly
fields.definition: "Polydactyly of the foot most commonly refers to the presence of six toes on one foot. Postaxial polydactyly affects the lateral ray and the duplication may range from a well-formed articulated digit to a rudimentary digit." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
synonyms: Extra toe attached near the little toe

fields.label: Diffuse mesangial sclerosis
fields.definition: "Thickening and scarring (sclerosis) of the mesangium (a structure in the glomerulus). The sclerosis affects a large portion of the mesangium across multiple glomeruli. Histologic features include an increase in the mesangial matrix, thickened glomerular basement membrane, tubular casts, and interstitial inflammation. Diffuse mesangial sclerosis presents with nephrotic syndrome at birth or within the first year of life. Glomeruli are small and condensed in appearance, with early lesions showing increased loose mesangial collagen that progress to sclerosis with dense collagen without hypercellularity. Podocytes do not show hyperplasia but may be immature and cobblestone-like. Electron microscopy shows extensive foot process effacement without deposits, but increased collagen within mesangial areas." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:26408240]

fields.label: Postural instability
fields.definition: "A tendency to fall or the inability to keep oneself from falling; imbalance. The retropulsion test is widely regarded as the gold standard to evaluate postural instability, Use of the retropulsion test includes a rapid balance perturbation in the backward direction, and the number of balance correcting steps (or total absence thereof) is used to rate the degree of postural instability. Healthy subjects correct such perturbations with either one or two large steps, or without taking any steps, hinging rapidly at the hips while swinging the arms forward as a counterweight. In patients with balance impairment, balance correcting steps are often too small, forcing patients to take more than two steps. Taking three or more steps is generally considered to be abnormal, and taking more than five steps is regarded as being clearly abnormal. Markedly affected patients continue to step backward without ever regaining their balance and must be caught by the examiner (this would be called true retropulsion). Even more severely affected patients fail to correct entirely, and fall backward like a pushed toy soldier, without taking any corrective steps." [PMID:25613349]

fields.label: Waddling gait
fields.definition: "Weakness of the hip girdle and upper thigh muscles, for instance in myopathies, leads to an instability of the pelvis on standing and walking. If the muscles extending the hip joint are affected, the posture in that joint becomes flexed and lumbar lordosis increases. The patients usually have difficulties standing up from a sitting position. Due to weakness in the gluteus medius muscle, the hip on the side of the swinging leg drops with each step (referred to as Trendelenburg sign). The gait appears waddling. The patients frequently attempt to counteract the dropping of the hip on the swinging side by bending the trunk towards the side which is in the stance phase (in the German language literature this is referred to as Duchenne sign). Similar gait patterns can be caused by orthopedic conditions when the origin and the insertion site of the gluteus medius muscle are closer to each other than normal, for instance due to a posttraumatic elevation of the trochanter or pseudarthrosis of the femoral neck." fields.label: Type IV atherosclerotic lesion
fields.definition: "In type IV atherosclerotic lesions a dense accumulation of extracellular lipid occupies an extensive but well-defined region of the intima. This type of extracellular lipid accumulation is known as the lipid core. A fibrous tissue increase is not a feature, and complications such as defects of the lesion surface and thrombosis are not present. The type IV lesion is also known as atheroma. Type IV is the first lesion considered advanced in this classification because of the severe intimal disorganization caused by the lipid core. The characteristic core appears to develop from an increase and the consequent confluence of the small isolated pools of extracellular lipid that characterize type III lesions. The increase in lipid is believed to result from continued insudation from the plasma. Type IV lesions, when they first appear in younger people, are found in the same locations as adaptive intimal thickenings of the eccentric type. Thus, atheroma is, at least initially, an eccentric lesion." [PMID:7648691]

The most common presentation is with ascites, but can range from fulminant hepatic failure (FHF) to asymptomatic forms. Obstruction of hepatic venous outflow is mainly caused by primary intravascular thrombosis, which can occur suddenly or be repeated over time, accompanied by some revascularization, accounting for the variable parenchymal hepatic damage and histologic presentation. Budd-Chiari syndrome is thus a disease, but since it occurs as a manifestation of several other diseases, this term is kept for the present for convenience." fields.label: Rickets
fields.definition: "Rickets is divided into two major categories including calcipenic and phosphopenic. Hypophosphatemia is described as a common manifestation of both categories. Hypophosphatemic rickets is the most common type of rickets that is characterized by low levels of serum phosphate, resistance to ultraviolet radiation or vitamin D intake. There are several issues involved in hypophosphatemic rickets such as calcium, vitamin D, phosphorus deficiencies. Moreover, other disorder can be associated with its occurrence such as absorption defects due to pancreatic, intestinal, gastric, and renal disorders and hepatobiliary disease. Symptoms are usually seen in childhood and can be varied in severity. Severe forms may be linked to bowing of the legs, poor bone growth, and short stature as well as joint and bone pain. Hypophosphatemic rickets are associated with renal excretion of phosphate, hypophosphatemia, and mineral defects in bones. The familial type of the disease is the most common type of rickets." [GARD:0005700]

fields.label: Abnormality of bone mineral density
fields.definition: "This term applies to all changes in bone mineral density which (depending on severity) can be seen on x-rays as a change in density and or structure of the bone. Changes may affect all bones of the organism, just certain bones or only parts of bones and include decreased mineralisation as may be seen in osteoporosis or increased mineralisation and or ossification as in osteopetrosis, exostoses or any kind of atopic calicfications of different origin and distribution. The overall amount of mineralization of the bone-organ can be measured as the amount of matter per cubic centimeter of bones, usually measured by densitometry of the lumbar spine or hip. The measurements are usually reported as g/cm3 or as a Z-score (the number of standard deviations above or below the mean for the patient's age and sex). Note that measurement with this method does not reflect local changes in other bones, and as such might not be correct with regard the hole bone-organ." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

Tracheal diverticula are either congenital or acquired, in the latter case the most common causes are prolonged increased intraluminal pressure, e.g. chronic cough, COPD, tracheomalacia, and iatrogenic (e.g. post-surgical)." fields.label: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
fields.definition: "Hypersensitivity pneumonitis involves inhalation of an antigen. This leads to an exaggerated immune response and a following inflammation of the alveoli within the lungs. The main feature of chronic hypersensitivity pneumonitis on lung biopsies is expansion of the interstitium by lymphocytes accompanied by an occasional multinucleated giant cell or loose granuloma. After exposure to the provoking antigen, following symptoms can be seen: fever, chills, malaise, cough, hemoptysis, chest tightness, dyspnea, rash, swelling and headache and can be completely reversible, based on the duration of the illness, categorized as acute (HP:0011009), subacute (HP:0011011), and chronic (HP:0011010)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0113-912X, PMID:15316440, PMID:16635083, PMID:18051218]

Radiologocally would manifest as agyria or pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm." [http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q90573458, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:28440899]

fields.label: Duplication of thumb phalanx
fields.definition: "Complete or partial duplication of the phalanges of the thumb. Depending on the severity, the appearance on x-ray can vary from a notched phalanx (the duplicated bone is almost completely fused with the phalanx), a partially fused appearance of the two bones (bifid), two separate bones appearing side to side, or completely duplicated phalanges (proximal and distal phalanx of the thumb and/or 1st metacarpal). In contrast to the phalanges of the digits 2-5 (proximal, middle and distal), the proximal phalanx of the thumb is embryologically equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits, whereas the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the other digits." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Complete duplication of thumb phalanx
fields.definition: "A complete duplication affecting one or more of the phalanges of the thumb. As opposed to a partial duplication were there is still a variable degree of fusion between the duplicated bones, a complete duplication leads to two separate bones appearing side to side (radio-ulnar axis) as seen on x-rays. A duplication leading to an accessory bone appearing in the proximo-distal axis on x-rays, this is actually a different entity called a Pseudoepiphyses (see according terms) sometimes also referred to as Hyperphalangism." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Abnormality of the epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal
fields.definition: "In contrast to the metacarpals 2-5, the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5 (whereas the proximal phalanx of the thumb is equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits). The epiphysis of the first metacarpal is localized at the proximal end (as seen in the proximal phalanges of the other digits), whereas the epiphyses of the other metacarpal bones are located at the distal end. This term applies if the epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal is in any way abnormal, referring to age and gender depending norms, as seen on x-rays." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Ectopic accessory toe-like appendage
fields.definition: "In contrast to forms of polydactyly where the supernumerary digit (this can either be a rudimentary or a completely 'normal' digit) is either located postaxial (on the fibular side of the foot, next top the little toe), preaxial (on the tibial side of the foot, next to the big toe) or mesoaxial (somewhere central, between big and little toe), a supernumerary digit may also be placed ectopically, meaning anywhere else except post-,meso- or preaxial. In the literature this is sometimes referred to as Disorganisation-like Syndrome (OMIM223200)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Ectopic accessory finger-like appendage
fields.definition: "In contrast to forms of polydactyly where the supernumerary digit (this can either be a rudimentary or a completely 'normal' digit) is either located postaxial (on the ulnar side of the hand, next to the little finger), preaxial (on the radial side of the hand, next to the thumb) or mesoaxial (somewhere central, between thumb and little finger), a supernumerary digit may also be placed ectopically, meaning anywhere else except post-,meso- or preaxial. In the literature this is sometimes referred to as Disorganisation-like Syndrome (OMIM223200)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Primum atrial septal defect
fields.definition: "An ostium primum atrial septal defect is located in the most anterior and inferior aspect of the atrial septum. The ostium primum refers to an anterior and inferior opening (ostium) within the septum primum, which divides the rudimentary atrium during fetal development. The ostium primum is normally sealed by fusion of the superior and inferior endocardial cushions around 5 weeks' gestation. Ostium primum defects result from a failure of the fusion of the embryologic endocardial cushion and septum primum." [HPO_CONTRIBUTOR:DDD_dbrown, https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:40843896]
fields.synonyms_concat: Atrial septal defect, primum type; ostium primum ASD; Ostium primum atrial septal defect; Primum atrioventricular canal defect; Septum primum defect
