fields.label: Neuroepithelial cyst
fields.definition: "A benign epithelial-lined cystic lesion that can occur anywhere in the neuraxis. Neuroepithelial cysts are ependymal or epithelial lined fluid collections of unknown etiology within the central nervous system parenchyma with no obvious ventricular or subarachnoid connection. Most cysts are asymptomatic, however, some present with seizures, mass effect, or rarely with movement disorders. On imaging, they present as CSF-like parenchymal cysts with smooth, rounded borders and minimal or no surrounding signal intensity abnormality." [PMID:14672275]
fields.synonyms_concat: Glioependymal cyst; Neuroglial cyst

fields.label: Hepatic focal nodular hyperplasia
fields.definition: "Hepatic focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) is a benign hepatic tumor. FNH develops within hepatic parenchymal tissue that is otherwise histologically normal. Macroscopically, the tumor is characterized by the presence of depressed, grayish-white scar, which is generally (but not always) located at the center of the lesion, with fibrous septa radiating outward, toward the periphery of the tumor. This stellate scar is found in only 50% of all FNH nodules, but its presence is regarded as pathognomonic. The lesion itself is usually lighter in color than the tissue that surrounds it, and it sometimes has a yellowish hue. FNH nodules are generally not capsulated; their margins are well defined, and they are sometimes lobulated." [PMID:23396642]
fields.synonyms_concat: Focal nodular hyperplasia

fields.label: Increased bone marrow iron

fields.synonyms_concat: Bone marrow: iron stores increased

fields.label: Glenoid fracture

fields.label: Widened mediastinum

fields.synonyms_concat: Mediastinal widening

fields.label: Narrow mediastinum
fields.definition: "Abnormal decrease in the width of the mediastinum." []

fields.label: Ovarian torsion

fields.label: Septate gallbladder
fields.definition: "Septate gallbladder is characterized by the presence of a septum that divides the gallbladder in two chambers. When the septum dividing the gallbladder lies longitudinally it is called bilobed gallbladder and when there is a transverse septum separating the fundus from the rest of the gallbladder it is called an hour-glass gallbladder." fields.label: Esophageal myenteric plexus degeneration

fields.label: Rhabdoid tumor of the ovary

fields.label: Cardiac rhabdoid tumor

The cells are polygonal, with eccentric, vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli, eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions. The tumors have an infiltrative growth pattern, necrosis, and high proliferative index. The immunohistochemistry tools of investigation facilitate differential diagnosis by showing loss of INI-1 expression, usually accompanied by germline mutations of the SMARCB1 gene. When INI-1 is still expressed in the affected tissues, a rhabdoid tumor with SMARCA4 mutations should be considered." [PMID:35883926]

fields.label: Cortical myoclonus
fields.definition: "Cortical myoclonus mainly affects the distal upper limbs and face, which reflects the largest cortical representations of these body areas. It is often focal, but may be multifocal, bilateral or generalized, as a consequence of intracortical and transcallosal spreading of abnormal activity. It typically occurs on voluntary action and may affect speech and gait. Cortical myoclonic jerks are stimulus sensitive, typically to touch, but sensitivity to visual stimuli is also described. Most patients with cortical myoclonus have both positive myoclonus and NM, occurring either independently or together as a complex of the two kinds of myoclonus. If cortical myoclonus is prolonged and lasts for hours, days or weeks, it is called epilepsia partials continua and is considered to be a rare form of focal epileptic status. Focal cortical myoclonus almost always points to an underlining lesion of the sensori-motor cortex, which produces hyperexcitability (e.g. vascular, inflammatory or neoplastic)." [PMID:21339907]

fields.label: Pulmonary hemorrhage
fields.definition: "Pulmonary hemorrhage is a bleeding within the lungs. Older children and adults may spit blood or bloody sputum. Neonates, infants and young children usually do not spit up blood. Anemia, pulmonary infiltrates, increasingling bloody return on BAL and the presence of hemosiderin-laden macrophages in broncho-alveolar lavage (BAL) fluid or lung biopsy can diagnose lung bleeding. Alveolar macrophages contain phagocytosed red blood cells and stain positive for hemosiderin, a product of hemoglobin degradation, after about 48-72 hours following pulmonary hemorraghe. Previous or recurrent bleeding can thus be distinguished from fresh events. A differentiation into local or diffuse is of importance. Also differentiate if pulmonary hemorrhage is due to a primary lung disorder or a manifestation of a systemic disease." [PMID:16473816]

fields.label: Reduced insulin like growth factor binding protein acid labile subunit concentration

fields.label: HbS hemoglobin
fields.definition: "Presence of an abnormal type of hemoglobin characterized by the substitution of a glutamic acid residue at position 7 following the initial methionine residue by a valine (the mutation causative of sickle cell disease). The mutation promotes the polymerization of the HbS under conditions of low oxygen concentration. HbS can be identified by multiple methodologies including hemoglobin electrophoresis and high-performance liquid chromatography." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:34406727, PMID:3953566]
fields.synonyms_concat: HbS haemoglobin

fields.label: Increased HbA2 hemoglobin
fields.definition: "An elevated concentration in the blood of hemoglobin A2 (HbA2), which is a normal variant of hemoglobin A that consists of two alpha and two delta chains and is normally present at low levels in adults but may be increased in beta thalassemia." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199, PMID:26372049]
fields.synonyms_concat: Increased haemoglobin A2; Increased HbA2 haemoglobin; Increased hemoglobin A2

fields.label: Abnormal DLCO
fields.definition: "An abnormal amount of oxygen passes into the blood from the lungs and/or an abnormal amount of carbon dioxide passes from the blood into the lungs." [PMID:32310609]
synonyms: Abnormal transfer factor of the lung for carbon monoxide
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal diffusing capacity; Abnormal TLCO; Abnormal transfer factor of the lung for carbon monoxide

fields.label: Increased DLCO
fields.definition: "Increased ability of the lungs to transfer gas from inspired air to the bloodstream as measured by the diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO) test." [PMID:32310609]
fields.synonyms_concat: Increased diffusing capacity

fields.label: Decreased DLCO

fields.synonyms_concat: Decreased diffusing capacity

fields.synonyms_concat: Tiger tail banding; Tiger-tail banding

Generation of DCP is thought to be a result of an acquired defect in the post- translational carboxylation of the prothrombin precursor in malignant cells." fields.label: Abnormality of body mass index

fields.synonyms_concat: Knee joint over-flexibility

fields.label: Clinical relevance
fields.definition: "Subontology for annotating phenotypic features as distinctive or minor findings in patients. The subontology is intended to be used to annotate subjective clinical impressions of whether a certain finding is important for the differential diagnosis." []

fields.label: Distinctive finding
fields.definition: "In clinical parlance, findings are occasionally interpreted as being distinctive or minor, reflecting a subjective clinical impression of the importance of a feature for the differential diagnosis. A minor finding is taken to be one that is likely to have high utility in distinguishing the correct diagnosis from other candidates in the differential." []

fields.label: Minor finding
fields.definition: "In clinical parlance, findings are occasionally interpreted as being distinctive or minor, reflecting a subjective clinical impression of the importance of a feature for the differential diagnosis. A minor finding is taken to be one that is unlikely to help distinguish the correct diagnosis from other candidates in the differential." []

fields.definition: "Bradypnea is referring to breathing that is abnormally slow." []

fields.label: Abnormal cervical spine morphology
fields.definition: "Any morphological abnormality of the cervical vertebral column." []

fields.label: Early onset of sexual maturation
fields.definition: "An early onset of puberty, in this case early does not refer to precocious." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Early onset of sexual maturation

fields.label: Malignant mesothelioma
fields.definition: "Malignant mesothelioma is a form of cancer that originates from the cells of the mesothelium, a thin tissue layer surrounding the body's internal organs. Malignant mesothelioma is almost exclusively caused by asbestos exposure, pleural mesothelioma being the most common form, affecting the lining of the lungs called the pleura. Other forms such as perioneal-, percardial- or testicular- mesothelioma are much rarer." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Pleural mesothelioma
fields.definition: "A malignant mesothelioma originating from cells of the pleura (the thin layer of mesothelium lining the lungs). Pleural mesothelioma is the most common form of mesothelioma." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Peritoneal mesothelioma
fields.definition: "A Malignant mesothelioma originating from cells of the peritoneum (the thin layer of mesothelium lining the abdomen). Peritoneal mesothelioma is the second most common form of mesothelioma after pleural mesothelioma." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Pericardial mesothelioma
fields.definition: "A Malignant mesothelioma originating from cells of the pericardium (the thin layer of mesothelium lining the heart)." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Testicular mesothelioma
fields.definition: "A Malignant mesothelioma of the testis." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Epiretinal membrane
fields.definition: "An epiretinal membrane is a thin sheet of fibrous tissue on the surface of the retina along the inner limiting membrane. It appears as a greyish semi-translucent avascular membrane over the internal limiting membrane (ILM) on the surface of the retina." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154, PMID:32809538]
fields.synonyms_concat: Cellophane maculopathy; Epiretinal membranes; Macular pucker; Premacular fibrosis; Surface wrinkling retinopathy

fields.label: Stahl ear
fields.definition: "The presence of a supernumerary, i.e. third, crus of the helix in the helix, arising at or above the normal bifurcation of the antihelix." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Additional crus; Third crus

fields.label: Abnormal mesentery morphology
fields.definition: "Folds of membranous tissue (peritoneum, mesothelium) attached to the wall of the abdomen and enclosing viscera. Examples include the mesentery for the small intestine; the transverse mesocolon, which attaches the transverse portion of the colon to the back wall of the abdomen; and the mesosigmoid, which enfolds the sigmoid portion of the colon. Cells of the same embryologic origin also surround the other organs of the body such as the lungs (pleura) or the heart (pericardium)." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of mesentery morphology; Abnormality of the mesentery

fields.label: Capsular cataract
fields.definition: "A cataract that affects the capsule of the lens." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Nuclear cataract
fields.definition: "A nuclear cataract is an opacity or clouding that develops in the lens nucleus. That is, a nuclear cataract is one that is located in the center of the lens. The nucleus tends to darken changing from clear to yellow and sometimes brown." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Yellowish cloudy center of lens; Yellowish cloudy centre of lens

fields.label: Cortical cataract
fields.definition: "A cataract which affects the layer of the lens surrounding the nucleus, i.e., the lens cortex. It is identified by its unique wedge or spoke appearance." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Posterior capsular cataract
fields.definition: "A cataract which is found in the back outer layer of the lens. This type often develops more rapidly." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Cerebral palsy
fields.definition: "Cerebral palsy describes a group of permanent disorders of the development of movement and posture, causing activity limitation, that are attributed to nonprogressive disturbances that occurred in the developing fetal or infant brain. The motor disorders of cerebral palsy are often accompanied by disturbances of sensation, perception, cognition, communication, and behavior, by epilepsy, and by secondary musculoskeletal problems." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Cerebral paralysis; CP

fields.label: Abnormality of movement
fields.definition: "An abnormality of movement with a neurological basis characterized by changes in coordination and speed of voluntary movements." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of movement; Movement disorder; Unusual movement

fields.label: Recurrent hand flapping
fields.definition: "A type of repetitive behavior in which the affected individual repeatedly waves the hands and/or arms rhythmically." []

fields.label: Conspicuously happy disposition
fields.definition: "An unusually happy demeanor over time, which can also be observed during inappropriate situations that should, for example, cause distress, fear, or anger." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Conspicious happy aspect; Happy aspect

fields.label: Overfriendliness

fields.label: Lingual thyroid
fields.definition: "An aberrant thyroid gland or Ectopic thyroid located at the base of the tongue, just posterior to the foramen cecum as a result of a failure of the thyroid to descend." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Accessory ectopic thyroid tissue
fields.definition: "Accessory ectopic thyroid tissue arising from remnants of the thyroglossal duct anywhere along the path of the thyroglossal duct tract." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Tics

fields.synonyms_concat: Tic disorder

fields.label: Motor tics

fields.label: Phonic tics
fields.definition: "Tics are defined as movements or sounds that resemble physiological motor behaviors, but are typically inopportune to social context and appear sudden, repetitive, and often exaggerated. Tic vocalizations commonly termed vocal or phonic tics may include any possible sound (eg, sniffing, coughing, throat clearing, whistling, or grunting), word, or sentence and are most commonly encountered within the spectrum of primary tic disorders, as Tourette syndrome." [PMID:31651053]
fields.synonyms_concat: Verbal tics; Vocal tics

fields.label: Pseudo-fractures

fields.label: Ectopic respiratory mucosa
fields.definition: "Ectopic respiratory epithelium presenting as a superficial lesion in the skin usually localized unilateral in the skin of the forearm and associated with ipsilateral hand malformations." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Sarcoma
fields.definition: "A connective tissue neoplasm formed by proliferation of mesodermal cells. Bone and soft tissue sarcomas are the main types of sarcoma. Sarcoma is usually highly malignant." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Cancer of connective tissue; Malignant connective tissue tumor; Malignant connective tissue tumour

fields.label: Leiomyosarcoma
fields.definition: "A smooth muscle connective tissue tumor, which is rare type of cancer that is a malignant neoplasm of smooth muscle. When such a neoplasm is benign, it is called a leiomyoma." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Fibrosarcoma
fields.definition: "A fibroblastic sarcoma is a malignant tumor derived from fibrous connective tissue and characterized by immature proliferating fibroblasts or undifferentiated anaplastic spindle cells." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Gastrointestinal desmoid tumor
fields.definition: "Benign, slow-growing tumors without any metastatic potential. Despite their benign nature, they can damage nearby structures causing organ dysfunction. Histologically they resemble low-grade fibrosarcomas, but they are very locally aggressive and tend to recur even after complete resection. There is a tendency for recurrence in the setting of prior surgery and the most common localisation of these tumors is intraabdominal from smooth muscle cells of the instestine." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Desmoid tumors; Desmoid tumours

fields.label: Osteoma
fields.definition: "Osteomas are bony growths found most commonly on the skull and mandible; however, they may occur in any bone of the body. Osteomas do not usually cause clinical problems and do not become malignant." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Recurrent singultus
fields.definition: "A contraction of the diaphragm that repeats several times per minute. In humans, the abrupt rush of air into the lungs causes the epiglottis to close, creating a hic sound. Also known as synchronous diaphragmatic flutter (SDF), or singultus, from the Latin singult, the act of catching one's breath while sobbing. The hiccup is an involuntary action involving a reflex arc." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Hiccup; Hiccups; Recurrent hiccough; Recurrent hiccup; Recurrent synchronous diaphragmatic flutter

fields.label: Hemiballismus
fields.definition: "Hemiballismus is a rare movement disorder that is caused primarily by damage to various areas in the basal ganglia. Hemiballismus is usually characterized by involuntary flinging motions of the extremities. The movements are often violent and have wide amplitudes of motion. They are continuous and random and can involve proximal and/or distal muscles on one side of the body, while some cases even include the facial muscles. The more a patient is active, the more the movements increase. With relaxation comes a decrease in movements." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Ballismus

fields.label: Calcification of muscles
fields.definition: "Deposition of calcium salts in muscle tissue." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Skeletal muscle calcinosis

fields.label: Meningeal calcification
fields.definition: "Calcium deposition affecting the Meninges." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Multiple central nervous system lipomas
fields.definition: "The presence of multiple lipomas located in the central nervous system." [PMID:26942290]
synonyms: Lipomas of the central nervous system
fields.synonyms_concat: Lipomas of the central nervous system

fields.label: Abnormality of the medullary cavity of the long bones
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the medullary cavity (medulla, innermost part), which is the central cavity of bone shafts where red bone marrow and/or yellow bone marrow (adipose tissue) is stored." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
synonyms: Abnormality of the marrow cavity of the long bones

fields.label: Metaphyseal dysplasia
fields.definition: "The presence of dysplastic regions in metaphyseal regions." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Senile plaques
fields.definition: "Senile plaques are extracellular deposits of amyloid in the gray matter of the brain." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Braindruse; Neuritic plaques; Senile druse

fields.label: Ectrodactyly
fields.definition: "A condition in which middle parts of the hands and/or feet (digits and meta-carpals and -tarsals) are missing giving a cleft appearance. The severity is very variable ranging from slightly hypoplastic 3rd toe/fingers over absent 2nd or 3rd toes/fingers as far as oligo- or monodactyl hands and/or feet." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Cleft hand; Lobster claw hand

fields.label: Preaxial polydactyly
fields.definition: "A form of polydactyly in which the extra digit or digits are localized on the side of the thumb or great toe." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Polydactyly, preaxial

fields.label: Postaxial polydactyly
fields.definition: "A form of polydactyly in which the extra digit or digits are localized on the side of the fifth finger or fifth toe." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Polydactyly, postaxial; Postaxial hexadactyly

fields.label: Mesoaxial polydactyly
fields.definition: "The presence of a supernumerary finger or toe (not a thumb or hallux) involving the third or fourth metacarpal/tarsal with associated osseous syndactyly." [PMID:19125433]
fields.synonyms_concat: Central polydactyly; Insertional polydactyly; Intercalary polydactyly

fields.label: Abnormal tendon morphology
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the structure or form of the tendons, also often called sinews." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal shape of tendon; Abnormality of the sinew

fields.label: Synostosis of carpals/tarsals
fields.definition: "The carpus consists of the scaphoid, lunate, triquetal, pisiform, captitate, hamate, trapezoid, and trapezium bones. The tarsus consists of the talus, calcaneus, cuboid, cuneiform, and navicular bones. This term applies if there is any fusion among the bones of the carpus or tarsus." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

Fusion of carpal and tarsal bones

fields.label: Lip pit
fields.definition: "A depression located on a lip." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Upper lip pit
fields.definition: "Depression located on the vermilion of the upper lip, usually paramedian." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Paramedian lip pit
fields.definition: "Depression located paramedially on the vermilion of a lip." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Paramedian labial pits

fields.label: Abnormality of dorsoventral patterning of the limbs
fields.definition: "An abnormality resulting from a defect or disruption of dorsoventral patterning that normally happens during early development of the limbs. A disruption of the normal development of the dorsoventral axis may lead to a variable spectrum of different phenotypic abnormalities that may affect the nails and or palmar and dorsal side of the hands and/or feet, ultimately changing the normal dorsoventral appearance of the affected limbs." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.label_normalized: abnormality of dorsoventral patterning of the limbs

fields.label: Hyponasal speech
fields.definition: "Hyponasal speech is when there is an abnormally reduced nasal airflow during speech often in a setting of nasal obstruction or congestion." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Branchial sinus
fields.definition: "A congenital branchial sinus is a remnant of the embryonic branchial arches and their intervening clefts and pouches that has failed to regress completely. Sinuses typically have their external orifice inferior to the ramus of the mandible. They may traverse the parotid gland, and run in close vicinity to the facial nerve in the external auditory canal." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Branchial cleft sinus

fields.label: Neoplasm of the colon
fields.synonyms_concat: Colon tumor; Colon tumour

fields.label: Gustatory lacrimation
fields.definition: "Gustatory lacrimation results from an aberrant innervation of fibers from the seventh cranial nerve to the pterygopalatine ganglion which are destined originally for the submandibular ganglion. This aberrant innervation leads to uncontrollable tearing while eating or in anticipation of a meal." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Diffuse cerebellar atrophy
fields.definition: "Diffuse unlocalised atrophy affecting the cerebellum." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Skin pit
fields.definition: "A small, skin-lined tract that leads from the surface to deep within the tissues." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Skin pit; Skin pits

fields.label: Periauricular skin pits
fields.definition: "Benign congenital lesions of the periauricular soft tissue consisting of a blind-ending narrow tube or pit." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Periauricular earpits; Periauricular fistulas; Periauricular pits; Periauricular sinus; Pits around the ear

fields.label: Ulcerative colitis
fields.definition: "A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that includes characteristic ulcers, or open sores, in the colon. The main symptom of active disease is usually constant diarrhea mixed with blood, of gradual onset and intermittent periods of exacerbated symptoms contrasting with periods that are relatively symptom-free. In contrast to Crohn's disease this special form of colitis begins in the distal parts of the rectum, spreads continually upwards and affects only mucose and submucose tissue of the colon." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Colitis ulcerosa

fields.label: Crohn's disease
fields.definition: "A chronic granulomatous inflammatory disease of the intestines that may affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract from mouth to anus, causing a wide variety of symptoms. It primarily causes abdominal pain, diarrhea which may be bloody, vomiting, or weight loss, but may also cause complications outside of the gastrointestinal tract such as skin rashes, arthritis, inflammation of the eye, tiredness, and lack of concentration. Crohn's disease is thought to be an autoimmune disease, in which the body's immune system attacks the gastrointestinal tract, causing inflammation." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Granulomatous enteritis and colitis; Morbus Crohn

fields.label: Chronic colitis
fields.definition: "A chronic inflammatory disease of the large intestine (colon, cecum and rectum)." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: Acute colitis
fields.definition: "An acute and self-limited inflammatory disease of the large intestine (colon, cecum and rectum)." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]

fields.label: EMG: continuous motor unit activity at rest
fields.definition: "Continuous electromyographic activity of motor units at rest, i.e., without voluntary movement of the muscles." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.label_normalized: emg: continuous motor unit activity at rest

fields.label: EMG: myotonic discharges
fields.definition: "High frequency discharges in electromyography (EMG) that vary in amplitude and frequency, waxing and waning continuously with firing frequencies ranging from 150/second down to 20/second and producing a sound that has been referred to as a dive bomber sound." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: EMG: impaired neuromuscular transmission
fields.definition: "An electromyographic finding associated with erratic or absent neuromuscular transmission with erratic, moment-to-moment changes in the shape of the motor unit potential (MUP)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: EMG: slow motor conduction
fields.definition: "The presence of reduced conduction velocity of motor nerves on electromyography." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: EMG: myokymic discharges
fields.definition: "The presence of spontaneous bursts of rapidly firing potentials that recur at regular intervals of 2-10 per second and are unaffected by voluntary effort. This is an electromyographic (EMG) finding." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Abnormality of pattern reversal visual evoked potentials

fields.label: Abnormality of peripheral somatosensory evoked potentials
fields.label_normalized: abnormality of peripheral somatosensory evoked potentials

fields.label: Delayed somatosensory central conduction time
fields.definition: "An abnormal increase (delay) in the somatosensory central conduction time (CCT), which can be measured from the peak of N13 to the peak of N20 (peak CCT) or from the onset of N11 to the onset of N20 (onset CCT)." [PMID:2446842]

fields.label: Amyloidosis of peripheral nerves
fields.definition: "The presence of amyloid deposition in the nerves of the peripheral nervous system." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Hypertrophied muscle fibers
fields.definition: "The presence of an increased amount of muscle fibers with an increased diameter. This feature can be ascertained by microscopic examination of a muscle biopsy sample. Together with fiber size variation and atrophied muscle fibers, and hypertrophied muscle fibers are commonly found in myopathies." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Muscle fiber hypertrophy; Muscle fibre hypertrophy

fields.label: Muscle fiber atrophy
fields.synonyms_concat: Muscle fiber atrophy; Muscle fiber degeneration; Muscle fibre degeneration

fields.label: Perifascicular muscle fiber atrophy
fields.synonyms_concat: Perifascicular muscle fibre atrophy

fields.label: Increased endomysial connective tissue
fields.definition: "An increased volume of the endomysium, which is a connective tissue sheath that surrounds each muscle fiber. Together, bundles of muscle fibers form a fasciculus, surrounded by another layer of connective tissue called the perimysium." [PMID:32508678]
fields.synonyms_concat: Endomysial fibrosis

fields.label: Motheaten muscle fibers
fields.synonyms_concat: Motheaten muscle fibres

fields.label: Muscle fiber inclusion bodies
fields.synonyms_concat: Muscle fibre inclusion bodies

fields.label: Muscle fiber tubular inclusions
fields.definition: "Unusual regions of densely packed membranous tubules known as tubular aggregates which present as membranous inclusions, derived from membranes of sarcoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria, containing miscellaneous proteins with a variety of enzymatic activities." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154, PMID:15113116]
fields.synonyms_concat: Muscle fiber tubular aggregates; Muscle fibre tubular aggregates; Muscle fibre tubular inclusions

fields.label: Muscle fiber tubuloreticular inclusions
fields.synonyms_concat: Muscle fiber tubuloreticular aggregates; Muscle fibre tubuloreticular aggregates; Muscle fibre tubuloreticular inclusions

fields.label: Muscle fiber cytoplasmatic inclusion bodies
fields.definition: "The presence of inclusion bodies within the cytoplasm of muscle cells. Inclusion bodies are aggregates (deposits) or stainable material, usually misfolded proteins." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Muscle fiber cytoplasmic bodies; Muscle fibre cytoplasmatic inclusion bodies; Muscle fibre cytoplasmic bodies

fields.label: Muscle fiber intranuclear inclusion bodies
fields.definition: "The presence of inclusion bodies within the nucleus of muscle cells. Inclusion bodies are aggregates (deposits) or stainable material, usually misfolded proteins." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Muscle fibre intranuclear inclusion bodies

fields.label: Ring fibers
fields.definition: "Ring fibers are formed by a bundle of peripheral myofibrils which are circumferentially oriented such that they encircle the internal portion of the sarcoplasm which is normal in structure and orientation." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Ring fibres

fields.label: Muscle fiber hyaline bodies
fields.definition: "Subsarcolemmal, eosinophilic glass-like regions in the cytoplasm of muscle fibers. Hyaline bodies show significant reactivity to myofibrillar ATPase after acid pre-incubation and with immunohistochemistry, show intense reactivity with only slow myosin heavy chain. Electron microscopy of the affected areas show a lack of myofibrils and a uniform, finely granular matrix, sometimes suggesting a filamentous nature, containing few scattered nuclei and mitochondria." [PMID:16018165]
fields.synonyms_concat: Muscle fibre hyaline bodies

fields.label: Cerebral cortical hemiatrophy
fields.definition: "Atrophy of one side of the brain, characterized by findings including thinning of the cerebral cortex, reduced volume of the cerebral white matter with abnormal myelination, and enlargement of the ispilateral fourth ventricle." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]

fields.label: Subdural hemorrhage
fields.definition: "Hemorrhage occurring between the dura mater and the arachnoid mater." [https://orcid.org/0009-0006-4530-3154]
fields.synonyms_concat: Subdural haematoma; Subdural haemorrhage; Subdural hematoma

fields.label: Epidural hemorrhage

fields.synonyms_concat: Epidural haematoma; Epidural haemorrhage; Epidural hematoma; Extradural haematoma; Extradural hematoma

fields.label: Cerebral ventricular adhesions
fields.definition: "Bands of scar-like tissue that have formed within a cerebral ventricle." []

fields.label: Cerebral germinoma

fields.label: Cerebral granulomatosis
fields.definition: "Cerebral inflammation involving a granulomatous response, i.e., a non-specific inflammatory response involving granulomas, defined as a compact organized collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes including epithelioid and giant cells." fields.label: Cerebral inclusion bodies

fields.label: Hirano bodies

fields.label: Lafora bodies

fields.label: Cerebral hyaline bodies

fields.label: Rosenthal fibers

fields.synonyms_concat: Aseptic epiphyseal necrosis

fields.label: Scleroderma

fields.label: Immunologic hypersensitivity

fields.label: Seminal vesicle agenesis
fields.definition: "A developmental defect characterized by congenital absence of the seminal vesicle." [PMID:24839497, PMID:30136289]
fields.synonyms_concat: Absent seminal vesicles

fields.label: Head impulse test has corrective saccade
fields.definition: "In a patient with nystagmus, The examiner briskly rotates the head of the patient while having the patient fixate on a target. A corrective saccade indicates the patient's eye will move in one direction and quickly return back to neutral position." []
fields.label_normalized: head impulse test has corrective saccade

fields.label: Positive CSF infectious agent test
fields.definition: "Any kind of test for an infectious agent in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) positive." []

fields.label: Positive CSF toxoplasma gondii nucleic acid test
fields.definition: "Detection of Toxoplasma gondii nucleic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) by a method such as polymerase chain reaction." []
fields.label_normalized: positive csf toxoplasma gondii nucleic acid test
fields.synonyms_concat: Positive CSF toxoplasma gondii PCR

fields.label: Elevated circulating plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 activity
fields.definition: "The activity or concentration of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal." []
fields.label_normalized: elevated circulating plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 activity

fields.label: Abnormal circulating plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 activity
fields.definition: "The activity or concentration of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 in the blood circulation is outside of the limits of the normal range." []
fields.label_normalized: abnormal circulating plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 activity

fields.label: Brain localization
fields.definition: "The pattern by which a phenotype is localized to or predominant in a part of the brain." []

fields.label: Frontal cortical localization
fields.definition: "Localization to or predominance in the frontal cortex of the brain." []

fields.label: Posterior fossa localization
fields.definition: "Localization to or predominance in the parts of the brain within the posterior fossa." []

fields.label: Subcortical localization
fields.definition: "Localization to or predominance in the subcortical region of the brain." []

fields.label: Parietal cortex localization
fields.definition: "Localization to or predominance in the parietal cortex of the brain." []

fields.label: Occipital cortex localization
fields.definition: "Localization to or predominance in the occipital cortex of the brain." []

fields.label: Tobacco use history
fields.definition: "History of use of tobacco products such as cigarettes." []

fields.label: Bartholin cyst
fields.definition: "A fluid-filled sac near the vaginal opening. A Bartholin cyst is usually unilateral, asymptomatic blockage of the Bartholin gland, which may lead to a painless swelling." [PMID:36760371]
fields.synonyms_concat: Bartholin duct cyst; Vulvar cyst

fields.label: Abnormal circulating hepatic transaminase concentration
fields.definition: "Any deviation from the normal concentration in the blood circulation of alanine aminotransferase or aspartate aminotransferase." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal circulating hepatic transaminase activity

fields.label: Reduced circulating aspartate aminotransferase concentration
fields.definition: "The concentration of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal." []

fields.label: Elevated urine succinic acid level
fields.definition: "The concentration of succinic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Succinic acid high in urine

fields.label: Positive CSF varicella zoster virus nucleic acid test
fields.definition: "Detection of Varicella zoster virus nucleic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) by a method such as polymerase chain reaction." []
synonyms: Positive CSF varicella zoster virus PCR
Varicella zoster virus PCR in CSF positive
fields.label_normalized: positive csf varicella zoster virus nucleic acid test
fields.synonyms_concat: Positive CSF varicella zoster virus PCR; Varicella zoster virus PCR in CSF positive

fields.label: CSF pathogen-specific antibody positivity
fields.definition: "Positive serology in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for a exposure to an infectious agent (i.e., examining CSF for the presence of pathogen-specific antibodies)." []

fields.label: Positive CSF nucleic acid pathogen test
fields.definition: "Positive (abnormal) result of a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) test such as polymerase chain reaction that is targeted against a nucleic acid sequence specific for a pathogen." []
fields.label_normalized: positive csf nucleic acid pathogen test

fields.label: CSF varicella zoster antibody positivity
fields.definition: "The presence of antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against a component of varicella zoster virus." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Anti-VZV IgG antibodies in CSF

fields.label: Reduced circulating interleukin 6 concentration
fields.definition: "The concentration of interleukin-6 in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal." []
fields.synonyms_concat: IL-6 low in blood

fields.label: Elevated circulating C12 acylcarnitine concentration
fields.definition: "Concentration of C12 acylcarnitines in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. C12 acylcarnitines have a twelve-carbon acyl chain." []

fields.label: Frontalis muscle overactivity
fields.definition: "Increased activity of the frontalis muscle, causing a characteristic staring and astonished facial expression." [PMID:16353177]

fields.label: Nasal dermoid cyst
fields.definition: "An ectodermal inclusion cyst containing skin and skin appendages; sebaceous glands, hair follicles, and occasionally sweat glands." [PMID:27895540]

fields.label: Elevated circulating complement C3 concentration
fields.definition: "Concentration of the complement component C3 in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal." []

fields.label: Abnormal circulating inhibin B concentration
fields.definition: "The concentration of inhibin B in the blood circulation is outside the limits of normal." []

fields.label: Abnormal circulating lipoprotein(a) concentration
fields.definition: "The concentration of lipoprotein(a) in the blood circulation is outside the limits of normal." []

fields.label: Positive blood infectious agent test
fields.definition: "Any kind of test for an infectious agent in the blood circulation positive." []

fields.label: Positive respiratory tract infectious agent test
fields.definition: "Any kind of test for an infectious agent in the respiratory tract positive." []
fields.label_normalized: positive respiratory tract infectious agent test

fields.label: Body odor
fields.definition: "A perceived unpleasant smell given off by the body." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: BO; Body odor; Bromhidrosis; Bromidrosis; Osmidrosis

fields.label: Anal pain
fields.definition: "Pain in and around the anus or rectum (perianal region)." [http://www.mayoclinic.org/symptoms/anal-pain/basics/definition/sym-20050918]
fields.synonyms_concat: Anal pain; Anorectal pain; Proctalgia; Rectal pain

fields.label: Urethritis
fields.definition: "Inflammation of the urethra." [PMID:26220178]

fields.label: Iris flocculi
fields.definition: "Multiple cysts along the pupillary margin that appear as spherical or tear-drop-shaped pigmented lesions or wrinkled masses emerging from the pupillary border of the iris." [PMID:27843899, PMID:7575269]

fields.label: Cornea verticillata
fields.definition: "Golden brown or gray deposits with a clockwise, whorl-like distribution in the inferior interpalpebal portion of the cornea." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Vortex keratopathy

fields.label: Dysplastic gangliocytoma of the cerebellum
fields.definition: "It is a rare, slowly growing tumor of the cerebellum, a gangliocytoma sometimes considered to be a hamartoma, characterized by diffuse hypertrophy of the granular layer of the cerebellum." [PMID:11073535]
fields.synonyms_concat: LDD; Lhermitte-Duclos disease

fields.label: Moon facies
fields.definition: "A rounded, puffy face with fat deposits in the temporal fossa and cheeks, a double chin." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Moon face; Puffy face; Puffy facies

fields.label: Abnormal gonadotropin-releasing hormone concentration
fields.definition: "A deviation from the normal circulating concentration of the normal gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH). Intermittent GnRH secretion from the hypothalamus acts upon its receptor in the anterior pituitary to regulate the production and release of the gonadotropins, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormality of GnRH level; Abnormality of gonadotropin-releasing hormone level

fields.label: Lack of gonadotropin-releasing hormone pulsatility
fields.definition: "Secretion of gonadotropin-releasing hormone that does not occur in a pulsatile fashion." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199]
fields.synonyms_concat: Absence of GnRH pulsatility

fields.label: Abnormal cardiac test
fields.definition: "Abnormal test result of cardiovascular physiology." []

fields.label: Abnormal cardiac MRI
fields.definition: "Abnormal results of a MRI for the heart." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal cardiac magnetic resonance imaging; Abnormal heart MRI

fields.label: Abnormal cardiac catheterization
fields.definition: "Abnormal results from the diagnostic tests resulting from cardiac catheterization." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal cardiac cath

fields.label: Abnormal cardiac exercise stress test
fields.definition: "Abnormal results of exercise on heart function." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal cardiac exercise test; Abnormal exercise test; Abnormal treadmill test

fields.label: Abnormal resting energy expenditure from metabolic cart test
fields.definition: "Resting energy expenditure (REE) can be measured with indirect calorimetry using a metabolic cart, which is used to measure the oxygen consumption (VO2) and carbon dioxide production (VCO2)." [http://emedicine.medscape.com/article/2009552-overview]
fields.label_normalized: abnormal resting energy expenditure from metabolic cart test
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal metabolic cart test

fields.label: Abnormal cardiac biomarker test
fields.definition: "Abnormal blood test results measuring creatine kinase (CK), CK-MB, troponin (TROPI), myoglobin, and/or cardiac enzymes." [https://www.urmc.rochester.edu/encyclopedia/content.aspx?contenttypeid=167&contentid=cardiac_biomarkers]

fields.label: Reduced brain gamma-aminobutyric acid level by MRS
fields.definition: "An decreased level of gamma-aminobutyric acid in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0169-8159, PMID:27388694]
fields.label_normalized: reduced brain gamma-aminobutyric acid level by mrs

fields.label: Abnormal circulating dehydroepiandrosterone concentration
fields.definition: "A deviation from the normal concentration of dehydroepiandrosterone in the circulation." [PMID:27979632]
fields.synonyms_concat: Abnormal serum androstenolone level; Abnormal serum dehydroepiandrosterone level; Abnormal serum DHEA

fields.label: Shoulder muscle aplasia
fields.definition: "Absence of shoulder muscles." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Absent shoulder muscle

fields.label: Aplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
fields.definition: "Absence of the musculature of the pelvis." []
fields.label_normalized: aplasia of the musculature of the pelvis

fields.label: Hypoplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
fields.definition: "Underdevelopment of the musculature of the pelvis." []
fields.label_normalized: hypoplasia of the musculature of the pelvis

fields.label: Aplastic colon
fields.definition: "Congenital absence of the colon" []
fields.synonyms_concat: Absence of the colon; Aplasia of the colon

fields.label: Cotton wool plaques
fields.definition: "Deposition of large, diffuse cotton wool amyloid plaques (CWPs) lacking a dense core and associated neuritic changes." [PMID:20460383]
fields.synonyms_concat: CWPs

fields.label: Abnormal hepatic glycogen storage
fields.definition: "Change in normal glycogen storage content." [PMID:26835382]

fields.label: Sclerosis of the carpal bones
fields.definition: "An elevation in bone density in one or more carpal bones of the hand." [PMID:21120491]

fields.label: Abnormal neuron branching
fields.definition: "Abnormality of the structure and branching of the dendrites of a neuron." [PMID:20404840]
fields.synonyms_concat: Aberrant neuronal branching; Abnormal neuronal branching

fields.label: Abnormal natural killer subset distribution
fields.definition: "Any abnormality in the proportion natural killer subsets relative to the total number of natural killer cells." []

fields.label: Nasolacrimal sac obstruction
fields.definition: "Blockage of the nasolacrimal sac." [PMID:17203310]

fields.label: Nasolacrimal sac granuloma
fields.definition: "A mass of granulation tissue in response to chronic dacryocystitis as polypoid formations or they follow accidental injury, from probing and as a reaction to retained foreign bodies in the sac." [PMID:13434546]

fields.label: Nasolacrimal sac papilloma
fields.definition: "Benign tumor of the nasolacrimal sac." [PMID:4352147]

fields.label: Nasolacrimal sac epithelial papillary carcinoma
fields.definition: "The malignant epithelial neoplasm with papillary growths in the nasolacrimal sac." [PMID:16253035]

fields.label: Conjunctival cicatrization
fields.definition: "An abnormality of the conjuctiva and ocular surface caused by conjunctival inflammation and associated with scarring." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123]
fields.synonyms_concat: Cicatricial conjunctivitis; Cicatrizating conjunctivitis; Conjunctival cicatricial conjunctivitis

fields.label: Dermolipoma of the conjunctiva
fields.definition: "A benign tumor composed of adipose tissue and dense connective tissue usually located near the temporal fornix." [PMID:25586714]
fields.synonyms_concat: Conjunctival lipodermoid

fields.label: Myopic astigmatism
fields.definition: "A condition where one or both of the two principal meridians focus in the front of the retina when the eye is at rest." [https://www.aoa.org/]

fields.label: Latent hypermetropia
fields.definition: "A term to describe when farsightedness is masked when the accommodative muscles are used to increase the focusing power of the eye." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Latent hyperopia

fields.label: Eyelid retraction
fields.definition: "With the eyes in primary position, the sclera is visible above the superior corneal limbus." [https://www.aao.org/bcscsnippetdetail.aspx?id=03ad3eb3-3445-4be2-9470-2c4845169b75, PMID:8719687]

fields.label: Upper eyelid retraction
fields.definition: "An elevation of the eyelid above the normal level in the primary position." [PMID:7735674]

fields.label: Collier's sign
fields.definition: "A unilateral or bilateral eyelid retraction due to midbrain lesions." [PMID:17323781]

fields.label: Seborrhoeic blepharitis
fields.definition: "Inflammation of the eyelid due to overactivity of the sebaceous gland." [PMID:10777824]

fields.label: Nasolacrimal sac lymphoma
fields.definition: "A type of lymphoma that involves the nasolacrimal sac." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123, PMID:9392338]

fields.label: Delayed canalization of nasolacrimal duct
fields.definition: "A very common condition in which the extreme end of the nasolacrimal duct underneath the inferior turbinate fails to complete its canalization in the newborn period." [PMID:11222337]

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity
fields.definition: "An avascular or abnormally vascularized retina that occurs in premature infants and can lead to blindness." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9, PMID:16009843]

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 1
fields.definition: "The retinal vessels stop and then a linear flat white line is present that usually runs the circumference of the vascular retina." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9, PMID:16009843]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP stage 1

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 2
fields.definition: "The accumulating neovascularization thickens and manifests as a linear bump. The neovascularization remains along the surface of the retina and does not extend off the retina into the cortical vitreous." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP stage 2

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 3
fields.definition: "The neovascularization accumulates at the edge of the vascularized retina and extends into the vitreous (also called extra retinal fibrosis proliferation). In cases of Zone 2 and Zone 3, this may be sausage shaped. In more posterior Zone 1 disease, the stage 3 can appear as a direct extension of the normal retinal vessels but extending tangentially over the avascular retina." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP stage 3

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 4
fields.definition: "Scar tissue that forms a continuous sheet coming up from the edge of the vascularized retina. This scar tissue can grow toward the vitreous base/posterior lens capsule resulting in traction, distortion, and even detachment." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP stage 4

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 4a
fields.definition: "A detachment that involves the peripheral retina that does not extend into the macula." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP stage 4a

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 4b
fields.definition: "A detachment that involves the peripheral retina that involves the macula itself. The detachment usually starts in the temporal periphery although can also involve the nasal retina as well." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP 4b

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 5
fields.definition: "Funnel detachment from the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP stage 5

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 5a
fields.definition: "An open funnel detachment of the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP stage 5a

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 5b
fields.definition: "A closed funnel detachment of the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP stage 5b

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity zone I
fields.definition: "Retinopathy which extends from the center of the optic disc to twice the distance from the center of the optic disc to the center of the macula." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9, PMID:16009843]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP zone 1

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity zone II
fields.definition: "Retinopathy which extends centrifugally from the edge of zone I to the nasal ora serrata." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9, PMID:16009843]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP zone II

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity zone III
fields.definition: "Retinopathy which is a residual crescent of retina anterior to zone II." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9, PMID:16009843]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP zone III

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity plus
fields.definition: "Venous dilatation and arteriolar tortuosity of the posterior retinal vessels and may later increase in severity to include iris vascular engorgement, poor pupillary dilatation (rigid pupil), and vitreous haze. This definition has been further refined in the later clinical trials in which the diagnosis of plus disease could be made if sufficient vascular dilatation and tortuosity are present in at least 2 quadrants of the eye." [PMID:16009843]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP plus

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity pre-plus
fields.definition: "As vascular abnormalities of the posterior pole that are insufficient for the diagnosis of plus disease but that demonstrate more arterial tortuosity and more venous dilatation than normal." [PMID:16009843]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP pre-plus

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity threshold
fields.definition: "A retinopathy with a 50% likelihood of progressing to retinal detachment. Threshold disease is considered to be present when stage 3 retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is present in either zone I or zone II, with at least 5 continuous or 8 total clock hours of disease, and the presence of plus disease." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP threshold

fields.label: Retinopathy of prematurity prethreshold
fields.definition: "High risk patients who were in Zone 1 (no Plus or stage 3) or Zone 2 with Plus or stage 3 but not both." [ISBN:978-3-319-52190-9]
fields.synonyms_concat: ROP prethreshold

fields.label: Latent myopia
fields.definition: "The difference between total and manifest myopia." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123]

fields.label: Paralytic ectropion
fields.definition: "A type of ectropion associated with orbicularis muscle weakness caused by cranial nerve VII palsy." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123, ISBN-13:9781416029076]

fields.label: Conjunctival dermolipoma
fields.definition: "A conjuctival lesion composed of adipose tissue and dense connective tissue. Such choristomas of dermal elements are normally found at the outer canthus, and have a gelatinous appearance. Classically, there is an indistinct posterior border (with the lesion frequently extending into the orbit) and a well-demarcated anterior border several millimeters posterior to the limbus." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123]

fields.label: Absolute eccentric fixation
fields.definition: "Eccentric fixation in which the angle of eccentricity equals the objective angle of deviation." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123]

fields.label: Abnormal ocular alignment
fields.definition: "Any deviation from the normal ocular alignment." [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7941-2961]

fields.label: Dissociated vertical deviation
fields.definition: "An incomitant tendency for an occluded eye to elevate and extort which resolves on uncovering." [ISBN-13:978-0199679980]

fields.label: Dissociated horizontal deviation
fields.definition: "A change in horizontal ocular alignment, unrelated to accommodation, that is brought about solely by a change in the balance of visual input from the two eyes." [PMID:18427617]

fields.label: Alternating hypertropia
fields.definition: "A type of vertical tropia in which, when one eye is fixing, the other eye is deviated upwards." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123]

fields.label: Alternating hyperphoria
fields.definition: "A type of vertical phoria in which, in dissociation, the occluded eye deviates upwards." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123]

fields.label: Alternating hypotropia
fields.definition: "A type of vertical tropia in which, when one eye is fixing, the other eye is deviated downwards." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123]

fields.label: Alternating hypophoria
fields.definition: "A type of vertical phoria in which, in dissociation, the occluded eye deviates downwards." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123]

fields.label: Pseudophakia
fields.definition: "The term pseudophakia refers to having an artificial lens implanted after the natural eye lens has been removed. During cataract surgery the natural cloudy lens is replaced by an pseudophakia intraocular lens (IOL)." [PMID:28358301]

fields.label: Optic nerve gray crescent
fields.definition: "Having a characteristic appearance of a slate gray area of pigmentation within the disk margins that commonly appears along the inferotemporal or temporal neuroretinal rim areas." [PMID:24862768]
fields.synonyms_concat: Optic nerve grey crescent; Temporal gray pigmentary crescent; Temporal grey pigmentary crescent

fields.label: Peripapillary atrophy
fields.definition: "Thinning in the layers of the retina and retinal pigment epithelium around the optic nerve." [PMID:20920826]

fields.label: Optic nerve sheath meningioma
fields.definition: "A benign tumor of meningothelial cells of the meninges that usually occurs in middle age. It is typically unilateral and there is an association with neurofibromatosis type 2." [ISBN-13:978-0199552641]

fields.label: Periocular capillary hemangioma
fields.definition: "A capillary hemangioma surrounding the eyeball but within the orbit." [PMID:20616917]
fields.synonyms_concat: Peri-ocular capillary hemangioma

fields.label: Lymphangioma of the orbit
fields.definition: "A hamartoma of lymph vessels that usually presents in childhood. It tends to increase in size with head-down posture and with the Valsalva maneuver. Superficial lesions are visible as transilluminable cystic spaces of the lid or conjunctiva that may also contain blood. Deep lesions may cause gradual proptosis or present acutely with orbital pain and reduced vision due to hemorrhage." [ISBN-13:978-0199679980]

fields.label: Orbital rhabdomyosarcoma
fields.definition: "A mesenchymal tumor that is considered to be the commonest primary orbital malignancy in children. Histologically, it may be differentiated into embryonal, alveolar, and pleomorphic types. It is usually intraconal or within the superior orbit." []

fields.label: Food allergy
fields.definition: "Primary food allergies primarily occur as a result (most likely) of gastrointestinal sensitization to predominantly stable food allergens (glycoproteins). A secondary food allergy develops after primary sensitization to airborne allergens (e. g., pollen allergens) with subsequent reactions (due to cross-reactivity) to structurally related often labile allergens in (plant) foods." [PMID:27069254, PMID:27069841]
fields.synonyms_concat: Allergic reaction to foods; Food allergy; IgE-mediated food allergy; Immunoglobulin E-mediated food allergy; Reaction to food allergens

fields.label: Latex allergy
fields.definition: "Latex allergy is an IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity response to natural rubber latex (NRL) protein with a variety of clinical signs ranging from contact urticaria, angioedema, asthma, and anaphylaxis." [PMID:15327474]

fields.label: Food-induced anaphylaxis
fields.definition: "Food-induced anaphylaxis is a severe, potentially fatal, systemic allergic reaction that occurs suddenly after contact with an allergy-causing food." [PMID:16461139]

fields.label: Venom-induced anaphylaxis
fields.definition: "A form of anaphylaxis that is triggered by exposure to venom." [PMID:21458655]

fields.label: Stool xenobiotic
fields.definition: "Presence of xenobiotic in stool." []

fields.label: Meconium xenobiotic
fields.definition: "Presence of a xenobiotic in meconium." []

fields.label: Hair xenobiotic
fields.definition: "Presence of xenobiotic in hair." []

fields.label: Plasma/serum xenobiotic
fields.definition: "Presence of a xenobiotic in plasma and/or serum." []

fields.label: Gastric fluid xenobiotic
fields.definition: "Presence of a xenobiotic in gastric fluid." []

fields.label: Decreased diastolic blood pressure
fields.definition: "Abnormal decrease in diastolic blood pressure." [PMID:21947466]
fields.synonyms_concat: Decreased diastolic BP; Reduced diastolic blood pressure

fields.label: Decreased systolic blood pressure
fields.definition: "Abnormal decrease in systolic blood pressure." [PMID:21947466]
fields.synonyms_concat: Decreased systolic BP; Reduced systolic blood pressure

fields.label: Isolated systolic hypertension
fields.definition: "Elevated systolic blood pressure without an elevated blood pressure." [PMID:21947466]

fields.label: Isolated diastolic hypotension
fields.definition: "A decrease in diastolic blood pressure (<60 mmHg) without a decrease in systolic blood pressure (> or = to 100 mmHg)." [PMID:21947466]

fields.label: Positive urine cocaine test
fields.definition: "Detection of cocaine or its major metabolite, benzoylecgonine, in urine." []

fields.label: Positive urine barbiturate test
fields.definition: "Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as Phenobarbital in urine." [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7941-2961]

fields.label: Positive urine cannabinoid test
fields.definition: "Detection of delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) or other cannabinoid metabolites in urine." []
fields.synonyms_concat: Positive urine marijuana test; Positive urine pot test

fields.label: Positive urine benzodiazepines test
fields.definition: "Detection of benzodiazepine metabolites, primarily nordiazepam, oxazepam, and temazepam, in urine." []

fields.label: Positive urine amphetamine test
fields.definition: "Detection of amphetamine or its metabolites in urine." []

fields.label: Positive urine opioid test
fields.definition: "Detection of opioids or opioid metabolites in urine." []

fields.label: Abnormal stool urobilinogen concentration
fields.definition: "Abnormal concentration of urobilinogen present in the stool." [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7941-2961]

fields.label: Increased stool urobilinogen concentration
fields.definition: "An increased amount of urobilinogen present in the stool." [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7941-2961]

fields.label: Positive blood barbiturate test
fields.definition: "Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as Phenobarbital in blood." [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7941-2961]

fields.label: Abnormal CSF urate concentration
fields.definition: "Abnormal concentration of urate in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)." [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7941-2961]

fields.label: Hypovalinemia
fields.definition: "A decreased amount of valine in the blood." [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7941-2961]
fields.synonyms_concat: Low blood valine concentration

fields.label: Hypotyrosinemia
fields.definition: "An decreased concentration of tyrosine in the blood." [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7941-2961]
fields.synonyms_concat: Decreased tyrosine in blood; Low blood tyrosine concentration

fields.label: Hypertryptophanemia
fields.definition: "An increased amount of tryptophan in the blood." [https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7941-2961]
